Recording a deed with the Wayne County Register of Deeds

Wayne County serves customers by appointment only. A visitor with up to five documents gets a 20 minute slot, while the 45 minute slots go to people filing five to 25. Daily slots start at 8:00 a.m. and the last begins at 3:50 p.m. Book on 313-224-5860, or call 313-224-5851 with recording questions.

The county's list of common rejections includes:

  • A photocopied signature where an original is needed.
  • A deed that names neither a consideration amount nor an exemption statute.
  • A first page lacking the 2.5 inch top margin, or type below 10 point.
  • Social Security digits left visible.
  • A warranty deed without the county treasurer's certification.

Transfer tax is accepted as cash, check or money order. Cards work for other charges with matching ID, but American Express and Discover do not. A check more than $25 over the amount due is returned unprocessed.

Frequently asked questions

Is there any way to close a Westland sale without the seller finishing the city inspection?

Yes. The buyer pays $80 for an Approval Letter to Close and signs the violations disclosure form with the purchase agreement. That opens a ninety-day period to complete repairs and pass the final inspection.

What fee does Westland charge on a Home Sale or Transfer application?

The rate is $250 for single-family houses, $475 for duplexes and $900 for multi-family buildings. The seller files it with the Building Division.

How long is a Westland Certificate of Approval valid?

Six months from issue, for a seller who completes the inspection. The furnace or boiler certification must be on file before final approval is granted.

Who pays Michigan transfer tax when a Westland house sells?

The seller. Wayne County lists $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, collected as the deed is recorded.

Does Wayne County require an appointment to record a Westland deed?

Yes. Daily slots start at 8:00 a.m. and the last begins at 3:50 p.m. For property tax amounts and due dates, ask the Westland Finance Department before closing.

Selling a house in Flint

Flint homes sell for far less than homes elsewhere in Michigan, so a seller's outcome depends on repair costs, liens and ownership history more than on the asking price. Flint is the Genesee County seat, about 66 miles northwest of Detroit on the Flint River, with 79,306 residents estimated on July 1, 2025.

A Flint owner has three paths: an agent listing, a direct sale to a neighbor or investor, or a buyer who pays cash and takes the house untouched. Each one runs into the city's rental ordinance, its water billing rule or county tax foreclosure in a different way.

An older housing stock

The housing stock was built for a much larger workforce. Population reached about 197,000 in 1960 and measured 81,252 in 2020, so a seller here is often marketing an older house to a smaller pool of buyers than the city once had.

  • Older houses can carry repair items such as roofs, wiring and plumbing that a buyer's inspector will list.
  • The Land Bank holds vacant lots and houses, so some occupied blocks sit beside empty parcels.
  • Tax foreclosure has shaped ownership here, so parcel history deserves a look before you sign anything.
  • The city had a lead-in-water emergency from 2014 to 2019, and buyers may ask what pipe work was done at your address.

Flint housing figures

Renters nearly match owners here, and the middle owner-occupied house is valued at $53,500.

At $53,500, a new roof or furnace can swallow a large part of an owner's equity. That is why many Flint owners weigh a quick sale of the house as it stands against the delay and expense of bringing it to retail condition.

Neighborhoods buyers ask about

Flint's neighborhoods are grouped around downtown, which is centered on Saginaw Street south of the river. Carriage Town and the Grand Traverse Street District hold preserved Victorian houses just west of downtown. East of I-475, Central Park and Fairfield Village sit between the University of Michigan-Flint and Mott Community College. East Village and the College Cultural Neighborhood on the east side are more stable, and the west side includes Mott Park and the Woodcroft Estates.

Public schools are run by Flint Community Schools, and Catholic and charter schools also serve the city. Ask your agent which school options matter on your street.

Rental rules and water bills

The rental ordinance matters if the house has tenants. Rental properties must be registered with the city and certified after an inspection. Single-family registration is a one-time $250, and the inspection is $225 every three years. Tenants make up nearly half of Flint households, and landlords must provide heat from October 1 through March 31.

The city also prefers water accounts in the owner's name, and unpaid water bills become a lien that can be added to the property tax bill. Before selling a rental, make sure the water account is paid and call the Building and Safety Inspections Division at 810-766-7284 to learn where the certification stands. Fees change, so request the current schedule.

Genesee County tax foreclosure

A delinquent tax bill can move a house into county tax foreclosure, and that is a real risk for owners of inherited or vacant property. The Genesee County Land Bank takes in properties through the tax foreclosure process: houses that go unsold at the public auction and are not claimed by the state or a local government are transferred from the County Treasurer to the Land Bank at the end of each calendar year.

Owners in the city can check parcel ownership through the city's property lookup, and a parcel listed under Genesee County LRC Inc or the Genesee County Treasurer is held by the Land Bank. Pay or arrange the back taxes before the foreclosure clock runs out, because a sale closed on time keeps the equity that an auction would not.

  • Get the exact tax balance from the county treasurer before signing a purchase contract.
  • Unpaid water bills can sit on the tax roll as well.
  • Ask the title company to pull liens early so surprises do not delay closing.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Flint houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Michigan transfer tax

Two Michigan transfer taxes apply: 55 cents for the county plus $3.75 for the state on every $500 of price, under MCL 207.504 and 207.525. The seller bears them, and payment goes to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered (MCL 207.523). The settlement statement gives the exact figure.

The buyer then notifies the city assessor within 45 days so that taxable value can reset the next year (MCL 211.27a).

When an as-is sale beats a listing

A sound house on a stable block can do well with an agent, provided the buyer's appraisal supports the contract price. When repairs would cost more than they add, or a lien, code order or tenant dispute clouds the deal, selling the house untouched removes most of the friction.

  • An agent listing suits a move-in-ready house when you can wait through loan approval.
  • An as-is buyer suits a house whose repair quotes outrun its likely sale price.
  • A neighbor suits an empty lot beside their home, a logic the Land Bank applies when it sells side lots.

Ask for proof of funds, read the closing date clause, and compare offers by what you keep after liens and costs. If the house is vacant, tell the buyer how long it has sat empty and whether the water is on, since both affect inspections and the price a buyer will offer.

Steps before you accept an offer

Pull the tax balance from the county treasurer first, then check the water account and, for a rental, the certification status. If the house was inherited, confirm who holds title and whether the paperwork is complete, because an unclear ownership history can stall a closing for weeks. Ask the title company to run liens early. With those answers you can tell a buyer exactly what is owed and what the closing agent will pay from your proceeds, and you can judge a cash offer against a financed one on equal terms.

If the house is empty, secure it and keep the utilities in a name you can manage until closing day.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Can unpaid property taxes be settled out of a Flint sale?

Usually yes, if closing happens before the county finishes foreclosure. The title agent subtracts the balance from your proceeds, and the Genesee County Treasurer can confirm the payoff and the foreclosure timeline.

Do unpaid Flint water bills follow the house?

They can. City rules let delinquent water charges become a lien added to the property tax bill, so a title agent will usually want the account paid before closing.

What does Flint expect of a landlord?

Rentals must be registered and certified after an inspection, repeated every three years, and landlords must supply heat from October 1 through March 31. Request the current fee schedule from Building and Safety Inspections.

Who pays the Michigan transfer tax on a Flint house?

The seller. The county charges 55 cents per $500 of price and the state $3.75 per $500, and the settlement statement shows the exact amount.

What is the Genesee County Land Bank?

A county entity that receives tax-foreclosed properties that fail to sell at auction. It sells houses and lots, offers side lots to neighboring owners and demolishes dangerous structures as funding allows.

Selling a house in Wyoming, Michigan

Wyoming, with about 78,600 residents, is a Kent County city on the southwest side of the Grand Rapids area, and only Grand Rapids itself is larger in West Michigan. Selling a house here involves the city Assessor's Office for transfer paperwork, the Kent County Register of Deeds in downtown Grand Rapids for recording, and a few city codes that surface during a buyer's inspection.

This page covers Wyoming, Michigan, which has no tie to the state of Wyoming. The sections run in the order of a sale: the local market, the city's rules, and the filings that follow closing.

The Wyoming housing market

Wyoming became a city in 1959 and grew up around manufacturing. The 28th Street strip is the regional shopping corridor, with new retail also toward RiverTown Crossings. The city has 21 parks on about 665 acres and ties into the Kent Trails bike network.

Manufacturing is the largest local industry, and the biggest employers are:

  • Gordon Food Service, 5,000 workers.
  • Metro Health Hospital, 3,000.
  • GM Components Holdings, 1,200.
  • ABC Technologies, 650, and Benteler, 580.

US-131 cuts north and south through the middle of the city, M-11 (28th Street) crosses it east to west, and M-6 touches the southern edge. Eight of The Rapid's routes serve Wyoming. Workers here report a mean commute of 21.9 minutes.

Eight school districts overlap the city: Wyoming Public Schools in the center, Godwin Heights in the northeast, Godfrey-Lee in the north, Kelloggsville in the southeast, Kentwood below 56th Street and east of the tracks, Grandville in the southwest, Byron Center near Metro Health, and a sliver of Grand Rapids Public Schools. Verify the district by street address.

Home values and ownership

The 2025 estimate of 78,588 residents is 2.7 percent higher than the 2020 base, up from 72,125 in 2010. Across 2020 through 2024, Wyoming had 29,417 households of about 2.61 people, and 67.1 percent of them were owners.

Homes occupied by their owners have a median value of $225,200. Gross rent has a median of $1,196 and household income $73,677. A typical owner with a mortgage spends $1,398 a month. Rising population and steady local employers mean buyers are active, so a clean certificate and complete paperwork help you close on schedule.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wyoming house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

City rules a Wyoming seller should check

Every rental in Wyoming has to be registered and certified, and the BS&A Online portal shows the status for any address. If you are selling a rented house, check that the certificate is current before a buyer finds an open violation. A short-term rental of 27 days or less must also register, at no cost and without an inspection.

Inspections, at 1155 28th St. SW (616-530-7285), issues building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits. Homeowners can apply online with no account, and most residential permits take one to two weeks. A buyer's inspector may flag these maintenance items:

  • Lawn grass or weeds over 10 inches.
  • Trash containers visible from the front of the house.
  • Cars on unpaved ground, or unlicensed vehicles outside a garage.
  • Fences in the required front yard taller than 36 inches.

Backyard hens are allowed by permit. The permit is free, caps a household at four chickens, bans roosters and free-range birds, and starts with a two-week comment period for adjacent neighbors, so a buyer who plans to keep hens should ask whether a permit exists for the house. Owners who want to split or combine a lot file a land division application with the Assessor's Office by the first Monday in October for it to take effect in the next tax year.

Filing with the Wyoming Assessor after a sale

The assessor tracks roughly 25,000 parcels and values them at 50 percent of the usual selling price. Taxable value is capped: it cannot grow each year by more than inflation or 5 percent, whichever is smaller. After a sale, the cap lifts in the following year and taxable value rises to match assessed value.

Each change of ownership goes on a Property Transfer Affidavit, due within 45 days. The title company typically hands over the form at closing. Leaving it out can trigger back taxes, penalties and interest running from the transfer date.

Recording a Wyoming deed in Kent County

The Register of Deeds for Kent County works from 300 Monroe Avenue NW in downtown Grand Rapids and takes cash, checks or money orders made out to the Register of Deeds. The charges are:

  • $30 for a deed, mortgage or other instrument.
  • $5 per deed for treasurer's tax certification of warranty deeds and land contracts, covering up to 25 parcels.
  • $1.10 per thousand of consideration for the county transfer tax.
  • $7.50 per thousand of consideration for the state transfer tax.

The seller or grantor owes the tax, and mortgages owe none. The deed states the full consideration, or a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit is filed at no charge. The office will not supply blank deeds or advise on drafting, so work with a title company or attorney.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wyoming houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Appealing an assessment

If you disagree with your assessed value, start with the March Board of Review. A missed March hearing is not the end: the Michigan Tax Tribunal takes residential appeals until July 31. The July and December boards only correct clerical errors and mutual mistakes and consider certain exemptions.

For a seller, this matters mostly for the buyer's first bill, since taxable value rises to assessed value the year after the sale. Hand the buyer your latest assessment notice so they know what to expect.

Putting a Wyoming sale in order

Check the rental certificate if tenants live in the house, and walk the yard against the maintenance list above. Gather permit records for any past work, then call the Inspections office with questions. Collect offers in writing, and for each one note the closing date and who covers transfer tax and title costs. Once you accept, the title company prepares the deed, adds the treasurer certification for a warranty deed, hands over the Property Transfer Affidavit form and records the deed in Grand Rapids. A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, which removes one common delay.

Frequently asked questions

What is the deadline for a Property Transfer Affidavit after a Wyoming sale?

It is due within 45 days of the transfer. The title company normally supplies the form at closing, and a missed filing can bring back taxes with penalties and interest.

Will the property tax bill on a Wyoming house change after a sale?

For the new owner, yes. The cap on taxable value resets to assessed value the year following a sale, and Wyoming assesses at 50 percent of the usual selling price.

Does a rented Wyoming house need a certificate before it sells?

The city requires every rental to be registered and certified, so a landlord should make sure the certificate is current. The Inspections Department, 616-530-7285, can check the status.

Which office records a Wyoming deed?

The Kent County Register of Deeds, 300 Monroe Avenue NW, Grand Rapids. It charges $30 per document, and a warranty deed also needs the $5 treasurer certification.

Can I still appeal a Wyoming assessment after the March Board of Review?

Yes, through the Michigan Tax Tribunal, which must receive residential appeals by July 31. The July and December boards only correct clerical errors and mutual mistakes and consider certain exemptions.

School districts by address

Rochester Community Schools serve most of the city, with Rochester Adams High School, Rochester High School and Stoney Creek High School all inside the city limits. Part of Rochester Hills falls in the Avondale School District instead, where many addresses are zoned to Deer Field Elementary in the city, while others go to Auburn Elementary in Auburn Hills or Woodland Elementary in Troy.

All Avondale residents attend Avondale Middle School in Rochester Hills and Avondale High School in Auburn Hills. Addresses in different parts of the city can belong to different districts, so get an official boundary check before a listing names a school.

Police, courts and city services

The city keeps no police department of its own, and the Oakland County Sheriff's Office provides police service. The 52nd District Court's third division sits in the city. The city runs the Rochester Hills Public Library and, by contract, lets residents of the city of Rochester and Oakland Township use it. When a buyer asks about services, send them to the city's website and the sheriff's office.

Forms for the Assessing Department

Two documents go to the Assessing Department at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive: a Property Transfer Affidavit and, for an owner-occupant, a Principal Residence Exemption affidavit. The city expects the closing agent to give the buyer both, and they can be mailed or dropped off during weekday office hours.

The exemption lifts up to 18 mills of school tax off a bill when the owner lives there as a main residence. Sellers should ask Assessing for the rescission form so the exemption on the old home ends cleanly. The department also handles exemption requests based on income, and those have to be refiled every year.

A buyer who wants a quick tax estimate can halve the estimated value and apply the current millage rate, or ask Assessing to run it. An owner who disputes a value gets one chance a year: the March Board of Review, after the February notice.

Filing the deed in Oakland County

A deed filed with the Oakland County Register of Deeds costs $30, which already contains the state's $4 survey surcharge. A discharge or assignment that cites several earlier recordings adds $3 for each extra reference, and copies run $1 a page.

The county treasurer must certify warranty deeds and land contracts first, for $5. When you mail the deed, the Register of Deeds can obtain that certificate if your payment includes the extra $5. Expect about two weeks to get a hand-delivered document back and two to four weeks by mail.

Transfer tax runs $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state. A deed with consideration under $100 is exempt, and any other claimed exemption must appear on the deed. The seller carries the bill under MCL 207.523.

Tax due dates around your closing

The summer bill covers school and county levies only. It is payable July 1 through September 14, and 1 percent interest starts September 15. Winter bills open December 1 and fall due in mid-February.

  • The city shows February 16, 2027 as the winter due date for the 2026 tax year, with a 3 percent penalty shortly after.
  • Anything still owed turns delinquent on March 2 and moves to the Oakland County Treasurer.
  • Postmarks do not count, so pay in person or online close to a deadline.
  • E-check payments are free online, while cards and mobile wallets add a 2.75 percent processing charge.

The winter bill adds the city's own levy for police and fire services, roads and the library, so a fall or winter closing can land before it is paid. Have the title company say who pays it and how it is credited, and use the Treasury tax look-up to see each parcel's status.

Preparing before you sign a contract

Look up your parcel in the Treasury tax look-up and note anything unpaid. Ask Assessing for the rescission form, and ask the Building Department whether any inspection applies to your address before you choose a closing date. Decide whether you will mail the deed or have the closing agent carry it in, since mailing adds time. Send the buyer's closing agent the legal description that matches your tax bill, so the county examines a clean document the first time.

A cash sale and the same paperwork

Selling for cash does not change the filings. The deed still goes to the Oakland County Register of Deeds, the treasurer still certifies a warranty deed, and the two Assessing affidavits still follow the closing. What a cash buyer removes is the lender: no appraisal gap, no loan approval deadline and no repair list demanded by a bank.

That can matter in a city where most houses are owner-occupied and buyers expect a clean, documented sale. Ask each buyer for the closing date they can commit to, then check it against the tax calendar above and the two to four weeks that a mailed deed can take to come back.

Questions buyers ask about the house

Expect questions about the school district, the tax bill and any work you did. Keep your Principal Residence Exemption records handy so you can explain why the buyer's tax picture will differ from yours. Bring permit sign-offs for any addition, finished basement or new mechanical work. If a buyer asks about services, point to the city's website and the Oakland County Sheriff's Office rather than guessing.

Where is a Rochester Hills deed recorded?

At the Oakland County Register of Deeds, for $30 including the $4 survey surcharge. Warranty deeds first need a $5 treasurer certificate.

Must a Rochester Hills house pass a city inspection before closing?

Ask the city's Building Department whether one applies to your address, and do it before you pick a closing date. The Assessing Department only handles tax forms.

What paperwork does a Rochester Hills buyer owe the city?

A Property Transfer Affidavit, and an exemption affidavit for a buyer who will live there. Both go to Assessing at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive.

What are the tax deadlines in Rochester Hills?

September 14 for summer and mid-February for winter, shown as February 16, 2027 for the 2026 bill. Oakland County takes over unpaid balances on March 2.

Who covers transfer tax on a Rochester Hills sale?

The seller. The county charges $3.75 per $500 for the state portion and $0.55 per $500 for its own.

Southfield's point-of-sale inspection

Southfield residential sales now run through a point-of-sale inspection, and that step sets the pace of a closing. City Council approved the program in April 2026 as Ordinance 1835, so schedule the inspection before you commit to a closing date.

A seller can go three ways:

  • Agent listing: showings, the buyer's loan and the city inspection all stack up on the calendar.
  • Private sale: you find the buyer and manage the contract with a title company.
  • Cash sale as-is: the buyer takes the house with whatever the inspection cites. Settle who pays for those repairs before you sign.

Because the program is new, ask the Building Department how it treats a sale that is already under contract, and keep the inspection report with your closing file.

How the inspection works and what it costs

The Building and Safety Engineering department inspects the house and issues a Certificate of Occupancy after violations are cleared. Its Point of Sale packet walks through the steps, and you apply on the city's online BS&A portal.

Southfield resale inspection fee, $190 total
Fee componentAmount
Application$40
Certificate$50
Building trade, reinspection included$100
  • Payment comes first. Staff then book the visit within 14 days of the payment date.
  • A person has to stay at the house for the whole window, either 9:30 to 12:30 or 12:30 to 3:30.
  • Sellers can repair the listed items and ask for a follow-up visit, which the fee covers.
  • Alternatively, buyer and seller both sign an Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations before closing, and the buyer gets 30 days afterward to finish the work.

The affidavit calls for a performance bond sized to the repairs and bars occupancy until the work passes reinspection. Life safety items must be corrected before anyone moves in. The Building Department answers questions at 248-796-4100.

Southfield housing snapshot

Southfield is about 15 miles northwest of downtown Detroit, with a July 2025 estimate of 76,111 residents. Owners live in only 53.4 percent of housing units, which makes rentals common. The typical owner-occupied home is worth $236,200 and typical gross rent is $1,340. Owner monthly cost is $1,779 with a mortgage and $764 without. The city has 34,860 households with a median income of $68,166.

Lathrup Village, a separate city, sits as an enclave inside the eastern part of Southfield. The main streets form a one-mile grid, with 9 through 12 Mile Roads running east to west and Telegraph, Lahser, Evergreen and Greenfield north to south. M-10 (the Lodge), I-696, M-39 and US-24 cross the city, and SMART buses cover local and regional lines.

Southfield Public Schools runs the city's schools. Part of the north sends students to Birmingham and the southeast corner to Oak Park, so confirm a street with the district.

Preparing a Southfield house for the inspection

Phone the Building Department and ask what the inspector reviews at your address. Check the file for permits that were pulled and never closed out. The packet includes a Furnace / Boiler Certification form with carbon monoxide readings, so a city-registered contractor should service the heating system first.

The 14-day scheduling window only starts after payment, so pay early. Collect your deed, payoff figure and permit records for the title company, and draft the repair affidavit ahead of time if the buyer will take on the work.

Recording at the Oakland County Register of Deeds

Oakland County's Register of Deeds in Pontiac (248-858-0597) takes the deed after the county Treasurer's Office has certified taxes on any warranty deed, warranty-clause deed or land contract. The office asks for original signatures, a notary acknowledgment on Michigan documents, the buyer's address on the deed and a 2.5 inch top margin on page one.

Call the office for the current recording fee and the county transfer tax rate before you pick a closing date.

Vacant or rented houses

The Building Department's forms include a Rental Registration form, a Vacant Building Registration Application and vacant building owner and purchaser affidavits. Ask which ones apply to your address before you list.

A rented house adds scheduling work, since someone has to be present for the inspection. A vacant house should be secured, heated in cold months and cleared of debris, so the inspector sees its true condition.

Timeline from contract to closing

Pay the inspection fee as soon as you sign a contract, because the 14-day window runs from the payment date. After the visit, decide whether to fix the cited items yourself or let the buyer assume them through the affidavit. Meanwhile the title company orders the tax certification and prepares the deed. Close only after the Certificate of Occupancy is issued or the affidavit and bond are in place. Keep every receipt and the inspection report in one folder so the title company and the buyer see the same record, and ask the Building Department before closing whether anything is still open on the address.

What the inspector looks for

Ask the Building Department for the Point of Sale packet and read the checklist before you pay. Inspectors cite life safety items first, and those must be corrected before anyone moves in. Heating equipment gets special attention, which is why the packet carries the Furnace / Boiler Certification form with carbon monoxide readings.

Walk the house yourself with the checklist. Look at smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, stair rails, electrical covers, plumbing leaks and exterior upkeep. Small fixes you make before the visit cost less than a reinspection request, even though the fee already covers one follow-up.

Who pays for repairs

The contract decides who pays. In an agent sale, the buyer's lender may insist that the seller fix the cited items. In a cash sale, the buyer may accept the house as it stands and sign the Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations, then finish the work within 30 days with a performance bond in place. Whatever you agree, get it in writing and keep the signed affidavit and the inspection report in your closing file.

If the house is rented, schedule a time when the tenant or a representative can stay for the full window. If it is vacant, arrange for someone to open the house and stay.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Documents to collect

Gather the deed, your mortgage payoff figure, permit records and any contractor receipts for recent work. Ask the title company which tax certification it needs from the Oakland County Treasurer's Office, since warranty deeds and land contracts need one before recording. Keep the Certificate of Occupancy with the deed copy once the city issues it, and hand a copy to the buyer. Write down the date each fee was paid so you can answer any question the title company raises later.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an inspection before selling in Southfield?

Yes. Ordinance 1835, approved in April 2026, calls for point-of-sale inspections on residential homes. The fee is $190, and a Certificate of Occupancy follows once violations are fixed.

Can the buyer take over the inspector's repair list?

Yes. Both parties sign an Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations before closing. The buyer then has 30 days to finish repairs, and a performance bond is required.

How soon does Southfield schedule the inspection?

Within 14 days of payment. A person must stay at the house through the full morning or afternoon window.

Where do I record a Southfield deed?

Oakland County's Register of Deeds, at 248-858-0597. A warranty deed or land contract needs certification from the county Treasurer's Office before it is recorded.

Does paying cash avoid the Southfield inspection?

No. Point-of-sale rules cover residential sales however they are financed. A cash buyer may take on the cited repairs through the affidavit and keep the closing moving.

The Kalamazoo housing market for a seller

Kalamazoo has a large rental population. The mid-2025 estimate is 72,683 people, and just 42.3 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Sellers here often hold a house near a campus, a former rental or a long-held family home, and the best route depends on which one you have.

A listing, a private sale and a cash purchase all pass through the same city desks: the assessor, the treasurer and the rental inspection team. After those are settled, the deed goes to the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds, which holds records dating to 1831.

Survey figures for 2020 through 2024 show a college town with mid-range prices. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $179,000, rent is $1,078, and there are 29,523 households of 2.25 people each. Estimates show a 1.2 percent dip in population from 2020 to 2025, so the market is steady. Only 75.9 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, which fits a place with many students and renters.

Schools, campuses and the Kalamazoo Promise

Most of the city is served by Kalamazoo Public Schools, with small sections in the Parchment, Comstock and Portage districts. Every resident graduate of Kalamazoo Public Schools has been eligible, since the class of 2006, for a scholarship covering up to 100 percent of tuition and mandatory fees for four years at any public university or community college in Michigan. That program is the Kalamazoo Promise, and buyers with children often ask about it.

Western Michigan University, Kalamazoo College, Kalamazoo Valley Community College and Davenport University are all in the city. Houses near those campuses are more likely to have a rental history, which brings the city's rental rules into play.

Neighborhoods and location

The city is commonly divided into 22 neighborhoods, and many have an association that works with the city's Neighborhood Development Division. Western Michigan University's West Campus, just west of downtown, holds the largest concentration of students. Downtown centers on the Kalamazoo Mall, and Kalamazoo sits midway between Detroit and Chicago on I-94, 50 miles south of Grand Rapids. US 131, M-96 and M-343 tie it to nearby towns, and the downtown Amtrak station serves the Wolverine line.

Put the block, the walk to campus or downtown, and any neighborhood association in your description, because buyers here shop by neighborhood.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Kalamazoo house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Rental certification when you sell a rental

The city requires registration and certification of every rental. After a passing inspection against the Housing Code (Chapter 17 of the city code), the owner receives a Certificate of Compliance. Inspectors may return at least every 28 months, and a courtesy notice arrives four months before expiry. Book the inspection about three months ahead and schedule any reinspection within 10 days.

Kalamazoo Certificate of Compliance lengths and conditions
CertificateWho qualifies
28 monthsStandard certificate for any rental, and the fallback when a property misses a longer one
40 monthsRenewals issued before the old certificate expires, with no appearance tickets or enforcement letters and six or fewer documented violations last cycle
52 monthsRenewals after two consecutive 40-month certificates, with no conditions and four or fewer trash or nuisance violations

Give a buyer the certificate's expiration date and any open violations. After the sale, ask the rental inspections team to update the owner on the registration form.

Tax calendar and deferments

The summer bill is mailed by July 1 and due July 31, payable whole or in six monthly installments. Skip the first installment and the city adds one 3 percent penalty, then 1 percent interest on the first of each month. The winter bill, mailed by December 1, is due February 14 in a single payment. After March 1, unpaid amounts are delinquent and go to the Kalamazoo County Treasurer.

A summer bill can be deferred to the winter date by owners whose household income last year did not exceed $40,000 and who fit one of these groups:

  • Age 62 or older, including an unmarried surviving spouse of someone who was 62 or older.
  • Blind, paraplegic, hemiplegic, quadriplegic, or totally and permanently disabled.
  • An eligible service member, veteran, widow or widower.

Applications reach the City Treasurer by September 15. Owner-occupants can also claim the principal residence exemption, which trims a yearly bill by over 25 percent. If you have a deferred bill and plan to sell, ask the treasurer how it gets cleared at closing.

What exemption paperwork changes when I sell?

When you leave, you file a rescission of your principal residence exemption with the assessor. A buyer who moves in files a fresh affidavit of their own. Michigan also lets someone who buys a second home keep the exemption on the first for up to 3 years if it is empty, for sale, unleased and not used for business. That conditional form must be re-filed each December 31. If you use that option, confirm it with the City Assessor's office before listing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Kalamazoo houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax on a Kalamazoo deed

Two taxes ride on the deed, and the seller pays both. Under MCL 207.525 the state rate is $3.75 per $500 of price. Under MCL 207.504 the county adds 55 cents per $500, because Kalamazoo County has under 2,000,000 residents. Payment goes to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered. Some transfers owe nothing under MCL 207.526: gifts to a child or grandchild, court orders that state no price, and deeds that only confirm existing title. Ask your title company which line fits your sale and have it shown on the settlement statement.

How the sale goes from offer to closing

The order of work is simple. Pull the last tax bills. If the house was rented, find the rental certificate and note its expiration date. Decide whether to repair before listing or sell as-is. If a buyer plans to rent the house, they must register it with the city, so give them the paperwork up front. At closing, the title company records the deed and collects the transfer tax. A cash purchase skips the lender and the appraisal, which helps when a house needs work or has tenants.

Bring a few things to the closing table: your deed information, the latest summer and winter tax bills, any certificate of compliance, and a forwarding address for later mail. Ask the title company who sends the assessor the paperwork after closing, and keep copies of every form you sign. If the house sits near a campus, tenants may have leases that run past the closing date, so read each lease before you agree on a possession date with the buyer.

Frequently asked questions

How often does Kalamazoo inspect a rental?

The city may inspect each rental every 28 months. Owners who renew on time and keep clean records can earn 40 or 52 month certificates with fewer visits.

When are Kalamazoo winter taxes due?

February 14, in one payment. The bill is mailed by December 1, and balances still open on March 1 are delinquent and payable to the Kalamazoo County Treasurer.

Can I defer my Kalamazoo summer tax bill?

Possibly. Household income last year must be at most $40,000, and you must be in a listed group such as 62 or older or disabled. Apply to the City Treasurer by September 15; the summer bill then falls due with the winter bill.

What is the Kalamazoo Promise?

A scholarship for resident graduates of Kalamazoo Public Schools covering up to 100 percent of tuition and mandatory fees for four years at any Michigan public university or community college, starting with the class of 2006.

What transfer tax does a Kalamazoo seller pay?

The seller pays $3.75 per $500 of price to the state and 55 cents per $500 to the county. It is due to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

Novi home values and population

Novi is a northwestern Detroit suburb in Oakland County, roughly 25 miles from downtown Detroit, and home values here run high. Interstates 96, 696 and 275 meet in the city and M-5 adds another link, so a house near one of those roads is a short drive from much of metro Detroit.

School districts and buyer demand

Shopping along Haggerty Road and Grand River Avenue, the Twelve Oaks Mall area and a large hospital campus all keep the city busy. Assessing department forms at a sale

The Novi Assessing Department answers at 248-347-0485 and handles four items you will likely touch at a sale.

  • Transfer affidavit: state law wants it filed within 45 days after the date of transfer.
  • Principal residence exemption: this takes up to 18 mills of school operating tax off a homeowner's bill. When the house sells, file the rescission form right away, because penalties and interest run back to the sale date if filing is late.
  • Conditional rescission: someone who moved into a new Michigan home can keep a conditional rescission on the old one for up to three years, as long as the old house is listed, empty, unrented and unused for business.
  • Board of Review: an assessment protest starts with a petition to the board.

City appraisers walk neighborhoods every year, and the State Tax Commission suggests that assessors inspect 20% of parcels annually, refreshing photos and sometimes measuring. A new deck, finished basement or garage will show up on the record card. Owners with low incomes can ask for a hardship exemption at the July or December board, bringing two years of returns and current account statements.

Permits and occupancy papers

Buyers and their inspectors ask about work done to the house, so permit history matters. Novi publishes separate applications for building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work, and an owner acting as general contractor completes the Homeowner Permit Policy form.

There is also an occupancy request form for new construction, and the Building Department needs two days' notice to process it. A temporary certificate of occupancy runs through the Administrative Board of Appeals. If you pulled permits for a kitchen, furnace, roof or addition, collect the final inspection sign-offs now. A change that affects drainage, such as a regraded yard or new patio, needs a Minor Land Improvement Permit, so check your records for one. The Novi Building Department can supply a copy of any record you cannot locate.

Recording at the Oakland County deed office

The transfer is recorded at the Oakland County Register of Deeds, reachable at 248-858-0597. Recording a deed costs $30.00, a total that folds in a $4 state land-survey charge.

Any deed with a warranty covenant has to be tax certified at the Oakland County Treasurer's Office before recording, for a $5.00 certificate charge. The closing agent usually walks both steps over. Pages need a 2-1/2 inch blank strip at the top and a half inch elsewhere.

Transfer tax is 55 cents for each $500 of consideration to the county and $3.75 for each $500 to the state. Look for both lines on your closing statement before you sign.

Getting ready on your side

A few days of prep shortens the whole sale. Pull your last deed, gather permit sign-offs and any receipts for a roof or furnace, and ask Assessing which exemption forms you need to file. Then decide who in your closing team handles the transfer affidavit and the county filing so nothing is skipped or filed twice.

A buyer paying without a loan may take the house as it stands, while a lender behind a financed buyer can insist on fixes. Knowing which kind of buyer you have shapes how much repair work is worth doing at all.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer has no lender, so there is no appraisal waiting on a bank and no loan approval that can fall through at the last minute. Repairs are negotiated once, in the offer, instead of again after the buyer's inspection. You still need the county recording, the tax certificate for a warranty deed and the assessor forms, so a cash sale shortens the calendar but does not remove the paperwork.

When you compare offers, ask each buyer who pays for the recording, the certificate and the transfer tax. Put the answers in writing before you sign, and confirm the numbers against your closing statement. If you moved out and still hold a principal residence exemption on the old house, the rescission form should go in the same week the sale closes.

Frequently asked questions

Do Novi sellers have to fix things before closing?

No Novi rule forces repairs before a sale. Unpermitted or unfinished work is the exception, so ask the Building Department about permit history first. A buyer paying without a loan may take the house as it stands, while a lender behind a financed buyer can insist on fixes.

When is the Property Transfer Affidavit due after a Novi sale?

Within 45 days of the transfer. It goes to the city assessor, and your closing agent may be able to submit it for you.

Does the principal residence exemption stay with the house after a Novi sale?

No. The seller must rescind it with the assessor as soon as the home is sold, rented or left, and late filing triggers penalties and interest back to that date. A conditional rescission can last up to three years on a vacant, listed, unrented former home.

Which office takes the deed after a Novi closing?

The Oakland County Register of Deeds, not the city. Recording costs $30.00, and a warranty deed first needs a $5.00 treasurer's tax certificate, so most sellers leave the filing to their closing agent.

Which school district will a Novi buyer be in?

Most of Novi is in Novi Community Schools. The south side is in Northville Public Schools, a section is in Walled Lake Consolidated Schools and a small western piece is in South Lyon Community Schools, so check the district for your address.

Owners in Pontiac can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take an offer from a company that buys houses directly. The city is the Oakland County seat, which puts the deed office and the treasurer, who handle recording for every sale, nearby.

Usually the condition of the house picks the route. A sound property with clean permit records suits a public listing. A property with deferred repairs, an occupant, tax trouble or an inherited title often moves faster with a buyer who takes it as it stands. Pontiac housing and buyers

Pontiac sits between Auburn Hills, Waterford Township and Bloomfield Township, and older houses near downtown, including the Fairgrove Avenue Historic District, date from the auto-industry boom of the 1910s and 1920s. Housing is modestly priced. For 2020 to 2024 the middle owner-occupied value was $121,700 and the middle rent was $1,063. Owners occupy 46.6% of the housing, so a large part of the stock is rented.

The July 1, 2025 estimate is 62,077 residents, up 0.8% from the April 2020 base. The city has 25,617 households averaging 2.36 people, with a middle income of $44,329. Owners with a mortgage pay about $1,223 a month at the middle of the range.

Modest prices and plenty of renters mean small investors shop for Pontiac houses alongside people planning to live in them. A buyer with cash can skip the lender-driven repair demands that often come with older houses. Out-of-area buyers also ask which school serves the address, so confirm with the district before you list.

Winter and vacant houses

Snowfall averages 36.0 inches a year in Pontiac and the record low is minus 22 F. A cold, empty house puts pipes, roof and furnace under strain. If yours sits vacant, leave the heat running all winter and get the roof and gutters looked at before anyone tours it.

Zoning and historic district rules

Pontiac planning handles three applications worth knowing: Zoning Board of Appeals, Historic District Approval and Zoning Compliance. Exterior changes to a house in the Fairgrove Avenue district or any other historic area may need approval first, and a buyer with renovation plans will want to know what the rules permit.

The State of Michigan, not the city, permits curb cuts and driveways on state roads like Woodward and Telegraph. Changed a driveway on a lot that touches one? Keep that paperwork with your records. Oakland County's Water Resources Commission runs soil erosion control inside Pontiac, which matters for a vacant lot or a house with grading work underway. For anything else, ask Pontiac planning staff what applies to the parcel.

Selling a rental house in Pontiac

Inherited houses and foreclosure timing

Two situations call for extra lead time in Pontiac. With an inherited house, the title has to be traced through every recorded transfer, and any missing document needs to be found before a buyer's title company asks. Allow time for that search, because a gap can pause a closing for weeks.

With a looming foreclosure, the redemption payoff comes from the Oakland County deed office, and only a person with an interest in the property may redeem. Get the number in writing, compare it with what each buyer offers, and choose the buyer whose closing date lands ahead of any deadline. A buyer paying cash can often meet a tight date because no lender is involved.

What to gather before you list

Collect your deed, the latest tax bill and any permits for a roof, furnace or addition. If the house is a rental, add the registration record, the certificate of compliance and the tenant's lease. If the lot touches Woodward or Telegraph and you changed the driveway, include the state permit. A folder with these items answers most of the questions a buyer or title company will ask.

Call Building Safety, the planning office and the income tax office with your address in hand, and write down what each one tells you. That short list becomes your checklist for closing day.

Yes, but registration and inspection rules apply. Pontiac requires one- and two-family rentals to be registered with Building Safety and inspected at least every three years, and a buyer must re-register within 60 days of the ownership change.

What is the penalty for occupying a Pontiac rental before inspection?

The ordinance sets a $500.00 municipal civil infraction fine, and each day is a separate offense. The owner or agent must notify Building Safety before a vacated unit is reoccupied.

Which office files a deed for a Pontiac property?

The Oakland County Register of Deeds. A warranty deed needs a treasurer's tax certificate at a $5.00 fee first, and a deed recording costs $30.00.

Does heavy snow matter when selling in Pontiac?

Pontiac averages 36.0 inches of snow a year. Roof condition, gutters and a working furnace matter most, and an empty house needs steady heat so pipes do not freeze before the buyer's inspection.

What is the middle home value in Pontiac?

$121,700 for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024. That is a citywide figure, so compare recent sales on your own block before accepting an offer.

How a Taylor homeowner can sell without a long wait

A Taylor owner may hire an agent, locate a buyer privately, or accept cash from someone willing to take the house as it stands. The house itself often decides, since Downriver neighborhoods like Taylor hold many older, modestly priced homes where repair bills can exceed what owners expected.

The median home value is $152,600. An owner whose roof or furnace has failed may have no savings left to fix it first, and a direct purchase of the house as is becomes worth a look.

  • Agent listing: strongest price potential when the house shows well and a financed buyer can be waited out.
  • Do it yourself: saves the commission, yet you still need a purchase agreement, title work and a recorded deed.
  • Cash sale: no repairs or open houses, with the closing date negotiated in the contract.

One Taylor rule affects every route: the city wants a certificate of occupancy whenever ownership changes, as explained below.

The Taylor market

Taylor spans about 23.6 square miles of Wayne County and has 61,279 people as of 2025. Dearborn Heights is its northern neighbor, and Allen Park and Southgate touch its eastern line. I-94 passes through the north end, I-75 clips the southeast, and Telegraph Road (US 24) serves as the main spine. Shopping is concentrated along Eureka Road around Southland Shopping Center.

Buyer budgets drive this market. Two of every three homes have owner occupants, and the population is down 3.3% since 2020, so buyers have choices and price carefully.

Certificate of occupancy when a house is sold

Yes, Taylor requires one. Under Zoning Ordinance Section 25.06, ownership changes call for a certificate of occupancy before anyone moves in. One certificate covers a single owner's time holding the house and does not pass to the next buyer.

This matters when you accept a fast offer. If the buyer cannot move in until the city issues the certificate, a repair item raised in the inspection can hold up occupancy. Ask the Building Department at 734-287-6550 what an inspector will check, and whether anything on the house could fail. The department is at 23555 Goddard Road, and its building inspectors keep short office hours each weekday morning and late afternoon.

Exterior work such as fences, siding, windows, roofing and concrete needs a permit, as does interior work that changes structure. Painting, tile and carpet do not. No work can start until a permit has been issued, so pull permits for any repair you make before closing.

Your first week as a Taylor seller

Begin with a few calls and one printout. A short list keeps a quick sale moving.

  • Call the Building Department at 734-287-6550 about the certificate of occupancy and any open permits.
  • Request a lender payoff letter when a mortgage remains.
  • Collect the lease and rental certificate if tenants live in the house.
  • Choose whether a title company or an attorney will prepare the deed for the Wayne County Register of Deeds.

Each task is small, and together they head off most surprises in a buyer's title search.

Selling a rented house in Taylor

Rental houses carry their own paperwork. City code Article V, Sections 8-100 through 8-111, calls for registration and a rental certificate of compliance, which stays valid three years and must be renewed before it lapses. Fines run $150 for a first violation, $250 for a second and $500 afterward, and each day can count separately.

Give a buyer both the lease and the current certificate. A new owner inherits the same duties, so a missing certificate becomes that owner's first expense.

What a cash sale skips, and what it doesn't

A cash buyer doesn't need a lender's appraisal, so the wait for loan approval drops out of the schedule, and you can negotiate the closing date in the contract. The city rules still apply. The certificate of occupancy, the tax proration and the deed recording all happen no matter how the buyer pays. Ask the buyer early who handles the Building Department call, who pays the recording fee and whether any open permit on the house needs to be closed first.

At closing, expect the title company to pay off your mortgage from the proceeds, settle any tax balance, and send the deed to the Register of Deeds for recording.

Schools in Taylor

The Taylor School District has a single comprehensive high school, Taylor High on Beech Daly Road. Charter options include Taylor Preparatory High School, Taylor Exemplar Academy and Trillium Academy. Municipal buildings cluster along Goddard Road near Telegraph, and Northline Road leads to the Wayne County Community College District's Downriver campus. Name the school district in your listing, since families ask about it first.

Transfer tax and recording costs

Wayne County prints its levies on the register's page: county $0.55 and state $3.75, each per $500 of the price. The grantor pays them when the deed is recorded, and MCL 207.523 names the seller as liable. A deed qualifying for an exemption skips the tax, provided it cites the lettered subsection of MCL 207.526 or MCL 207.505.

Recording itself costs $30.00 per document since January 1, 2026: a $26.00 fee and a $4.00 state survey and remonumentation charge. Warranty deeds need a Wayne County Treasurer tax certification beforehand. The recording desk answers at (313) 224-5851, and the office suggests having an attorney prepare the deed.

Tax bills around a Taylor closing

The summer bill is due September 30, and the winter bill falls due in mid-February. A real property balance still open on March 1 goes to the Wayne County Treasurer, and a second unpaid year exposes the house to tax foreclosure. Taylor cuts the summer bill along a July 1 to June 30 year and the winter bill along December 1 to November 30, so closing proration follows those periods.

Homeowners 62 or older whose income stayed below $40,000 can defer the summer bill by applying before September 30. Delinquent water charges and unpaid ordinance citations may be added to a bill as special assessments. Taxable value uncaps in the calendar year after a transfer, so a buyer should plan for a larger bill. The assessor's number is 734-374-1315.

If taxes are owed when you sell, the title agent deducts the balance from your proceeds at closing, so ask for a payoff figure before you set the date.

Is an inspection part of selling in Taylor?

The city issues a certificate of occupancy to the new owner after any ownership change, and the Building Department at 734-287-6550 can explain what its inspector looks at.

What is the Wayne County cost to record a deed?

A flat $30.00 per document, effective January 1, 2026. Transfer tax comes on top unless the deed is exempt.

Does the buyer or the seller owe Taylor transfer tax?

The statute puts it on the seller. A purchase agreement can assign it to the buyer by agreement.

What if taxes are late when I sell my Taylor house?

After March 1 the balance sits with the county treasurer, and the title agent deducts what is owed from your proceeds at closing.

Are rented houses treated differently in Taylor?

Yes. They need registration and a three-year certificate of compliance, with fines starting at $150 for a violation.

Ways to sell a Dearborn Heights house

You can hire an agent, arrange a sale yourself with a buyer you found, or accept an as-is purchase from an investor paying cash. Whichever you pick, the Wayne County register of deeds records the deed, transfer tax is paid at recording, and the city asks sellers to complete a few steps of its own.

A well-kept house can sell through a normal listing. Deferred repairs, a deceased owner's estate or a tenant dispute often point toward a cash sale, since the buyer absorbs the condition and the closing timeline is shorter.

  • Listing: the biggest buyer pool, plus inspection and financing contingencies.
  • Direct sale: fewer fees, with more paperwork landing on you.
  • Investor purchase: as-is, a quicker close and a price that reflects repairs.

Dearborn Heights housing and buyers

Dearborn Heights is an inner-ring suburb about 12 miles west of downtown Detroit, packed into under 12 square miles. It counted 63,292 residents in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 4.1% lower, so the city is shrinking slightly. The average household has 2.76 people, and the 2020 count showed 24,076 housing units with only 4.9% vacant. Median age was 35.7, and about a quarter of residents were under 18, which favors family buyers who care about bedrooms, yards and school zones.

Flood zones and school districts

The southern part of the city lies in the Ecorse Creek watershed, where the area around the creek is subject to flooding, and the north drains toward the Rouge River. The Building Department posts a flood zone map, so check your parcel before you price the house. Buyers tend to ask about three items: the flood history of the lot, how old the roof and furnace are, and the school district. Have answers ready for each.

The city is split among five public districts, which makes the exact address matter. North-end residents are usually in Crestwood School District or Dearborn Public Schools, and south-end residents in Westwood Community Schools or the Dearborn Heights School District No. 7. A small part falls within Wayne-Westland Community Schools and Taylor School District. Put the district in your listing, since buyers who search by school filter on it.

What the city asks sellers to do

If the house is your primary residence, you must rescind the Principal Residence Exemption when it sells. The title company may hand you the Request to Rescind at closing, and if not, the Assessor's Office at 313-791-3460 can give it to you. This applies even to a quit claim deed with no title company involved.

Contact the Building Department at 6045 Fenton (313-791-3470) to learn which inspections the sale requires, since the city offers a residential certificate inspection application. Call the Water Department as well for a final meter reading.

Treat the three city contacts as a package. Each one answers a different question: the Assessor's Office handles the exemption and the transfer affidavit, the Building Department handles inspections and the flood map, and the Water Department handles the meter. Making all three calls in the same sitting saves you from learning about a requirement the week before closing.

On the buyer's side, the Property Transfer Affidavit has to reach the assessor inside 45 days of the deed. A late filing can cost up to $200 on a primary residence, and as much as $4,000 on other residential property.

Wayne County recording charges

The county's recording fee rose on January 1, 2026, the first change since 1996. A deed now costs $26, plus the $4 state survey and remonumentation fee, for $30 on each document, however long it is.

At the counter, tax is taken the moment the deed is handed in, and the office wants cash, a check or a money order made payable to it. Tax is 55 cents per $500 for the county plus $3.75 per $500 for the state, which works out to $8.60 per $1,000 of price, and the seller pays.

A warranty deed needs the Wayne County Treasurer's certification that taxes are paid before it can be recorded. Every deed has to name the price or cite the exemption statute, and it needs original signatures and a notary acknowledgment. Calling the Register of Deeds at (313) 224-5851 before submission can prevent a rejection.

When an investor purchase beats a listing

It fits when the house has problems a retail buyer would refuse, when a deadline looms, or when you would rather skip showings. Typical cases are a house needing mechanical work, an inherited property, a landlord ready to exit, and a home with open city inspection items.

Also think about the estate case. When the owner has died, confirm who has authority to sign before anyone talks price, because a deed signed by the wrong person cannot be recorded cleanly. An investor who buys inherited houses regularly will know this process, but you should still ask for the steps in writing.

Before accepting, get the offer on paper, find out who pays recording and title costs, and make sure the buyer will cooperate with the city's rescind and inspection steps. A second quote costs little and shows whether the first is reasonable. Ask also how the buyer handles the Wayne County Treasurer's tax certification, since recording stalls without it.

A short sequence for sellers

  1. Call the Building Department at 313-791-3470 and ask which inspections apply to your address.
  2. Check the flood zone map and gather any water-damage records.
  3. Ask the Assessor's Office at 313-791-3460 for the rescind form.
  4. Request a final meter reading from the Water Department.
  5. Confirm the treasurer's certification for a warranty deed and the deed's price or exemption language.
  6. Remind the buyer about the 45-day affidavit.

None of these steps is hard on its own, but they come from different offices, so start the calls early. A seller who has everything lined up can close quickly whether the buyer is paying cash or using a loan.

Frequently asked questions

Is a certificate inspection required to sell in Dearborn Heights?

The city directs sellers to its Building Department to find out which inspections apply, and it offers a residential certificate inspection application. Call 313-791-3470 before you list so you know what is required for your address.

Which taxes hit the seller at Dearborn Heights closing?

The county's 55 cents and the state's $3.75 on each $500 of price add up to $8.60 per $1,000. The seller pays it, and it is collected as the deed is recorded.

Who files the Property Transfer Affidavit?

The buyer sends it to the Assessor's Office, and it is due 45 calendar days after the deed is signed. A late filing can carry a fine, so the seller should remind the buyer at closing.

What if I buy my next home before this one sells?

Michigan allows only one principal residence exemption, so you must rescind the Dearborn Heights exemption once you move out. The new city may ask for a stamped copy of the rescind form before it grants an exemption on the new home.

Is a flood-prone Dearborn Heights house sellable?

Yes. Parts of the south end sit in the Ecorse Creek watershed where flooding occurs, so check the city's flood zone map and tell your buyer what you know about water in the basement.

How the lake affects selling a house in St. Clair Shores

Lake St. Clair touches nearly every part of a St. Clair Shores sale, from canal and lakefront houses to the flood-zone check that follows insurance quotes. Water covers close to 19 percent of the city, and part of the city lies in the FEMA floodplain, so learn your own address's status early.

The city sits in southern Macomb County on the lake's western shore, about 14 miles northeast of downtown Detroit, and has 57,872 residents as of July 2025. Three selling routes are common:

  • A listing with an agent fits a well-kept house and an owner willing to wait out a buyer's loan.
  • A sale by owner saves the commission and leaves contracts and title steps to you.
  • A cash sale as-is suits deferred repairs, tenants or an estate. Compare offers and note who covers which closing costs, who handles the deed and when you get paid.

The St. Clair Shores market

The city measures 14.40 square miles overall, with 2.72 of them water. About 14 miles of canals run mostly along the Nautical Mile, the Jefferson Avenue strip between 9 Mile and 10 Mile Roads that holds restaurants, boat dealers and marinas. Many subdivisions were platted early but built out after World War II, so older housing is common. Interstate 94 skirts the western edge through exits 224 to 230.

Population peaked decades ago: 63,096 residents in 2000, 59,715 in 2010 and 58,874 in 2020. Buyers see a settled lakeside community, so a clean, well-documented house and a clear flood status are what set a listing apart. Gather your survey, any insurance paperwork that mentions the flood zone and your permit records into one folder before the first showing, so a buyer's questions get quick, documented answers.

Neighbors matter when you describe a location. Roseville and Eastpointe lie to the west, and Harper Woods, Grosse Pointe Woods and Grosse Pointe Shores lie to the south across the Wayne County line. The area was part of Erin Township from 1843 to 1911 and then of Lake Township, so older records may carry those names. Ask the title company to search under them if a document looks incomplete.

Floodplain checks before you list

FEMA redraws its maps now and then, so a parcel once in the floodplain may now be outside it, and the reverse can happen. Buyers often ask about flood status, since insurers and lenders look at it.

The city names two lookup tools:

  • Macomb County GIS: type the address, open Layers, expand Natural Features and tick Flood Zones. A parcel that turns red may be in the zone.

If an insurer has placed the house in the floodplain and you hold a survey or other evidence against it, you may qualify for a Letter of Map Amendment, or you can use the city's Options to Appeal Determination form. Sorting this out before listing spares you a surprise during a buyer's loan review.

Which school districts do buyers ask about?

Three public districts share the city. South Lake Schools covers the south, Lakeview Public Schools the middle and Lake Shore Public Schools the north, and each runs a high school inside the city limits. Ask the districts to confirm a specific address, because buyers want that detail.

Private options include St. Isaac Jogues and St. Joan of Arc, while St. Germaine closed in 2024. I-94 and Jefferson Avenue carry most commuters, and the average trip to work is 26.7 minutes.

Rules for rental houses

The city wants every non-owner-occupied house registered and holding a certificate of approval before anyone moves in. Its registration form prints these terms:

  • Single-family house: $150 for the first 3,000 square feet, then $10 for each added 1,000 square feet.
  • Multiple-family building: $150 for the first unit, then $50 for each added unit in that building.
  • The fee pays for the first inspection and one follow-up. A rescheduled visit when nobody is on site costs $30, and a failed-compliance reinspection costs half the original fee.
  • An owner who lives beyond Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Washtenaw and St. Clair counties must name a local agent.
  • Once the house sells, send the city a recorded deed or land contract to be dropped from its records.

Community Development and Inspections, at 586-447-3340, can confirm what applies to your address and whether an open permit needs closing before a sale.

Recording fees at the Macomb County Register of Deeds

The Register of Deeds in Mount Clemens, on N. Main Street, records deeds for a $30 fee however many pages they run. Of that amount, $4 supports the state survey and remonumentation fund. Call (586) 469-7953 with questions.

A tax certificate from the County Treasurer must come first for warranty deeds and land contracts, along with their covenant-clause and assignment variants. It costs $5 for up to five legal descriptions.

The county's transfer tax table multiplies the sale price by 0.0075 for the state and by 0.0011 for the county. Your title company can turn those rates into a dollar total at your price.

After closing, the buyer reports the change of ownership to the assessor on Form 2766 inside 45 days.

A simple order of steps for a quick sale

Start by checking your address in the flood tools, so you know the answer before a buyer asks. Print the result and keep it with your other sale papers. If the house is rented, confirm the registration and certificate of approval are current, and call Community Development and Inspections about any open permit. Then collect offers, and for each one note the price, the closing date and who pays which closing costs.

Once you accept, ask the title company to order the tax certificate if the deed is a warranty deed, confirm the transfer tax at your actual price, and record the deed in Mount Clemens. What do recording and transfer tax cost on a Macomb sale?

Recording is $30 per document. The county schedule lists state transfer tax at 0.0075 of the sale price and county tax at 0.0011.

Do rental houses have to be registered in St. Clair Shores?

Yes. Registration and a certificate of approval come before occupancy, and a single-family house starts at $150 for the first 3,000 square feet.

Which school district serves my street?

South Lake Schools serves the south, Lakeview Public Schools the middle and Lake Shore Public Schools the north. Confirm your address with the district.

How big is the city?

St. Clair Shores covers 14.40 square miles in total, with 2.72 of water, and the 2020 count was 58,874 residents.

How a Royal Oak sale works

Sellers here deal with the city's Assessing and Building divisions and the Oakland County Register of Deeds, and one variable is whether the house is a registered rental. An owner-occupied house needs the deed, the transfer affidavits and the tax steps, while a rental adds city registration and inspection rules.

Royal Oak lies on the Woodward Corridor roughly 10 miles north of downtown Detroit, within easy reach of I-75 and I-696. Many buyers want to be near the restaurants and nightlife around Main Street and Washington Avenue. Expect questions on noise, parking and event traffic, and answer them honestly for event weekends. Older streets have a mature tree canopy, so photograph the yard in full leaf.

Royal Oak values and population

Federal figures for 2020 to 2024 put the middle owner-occupied home at $328,700, with owners in 68.0 percent of homes and rent at $1,381. Household income is $101,109 at the midpoint.

Households run small, averaging 1.98 people, and 42.3 percent of 2020 households held one person. The population was an estimated 57,583 in July 2025, 1.1 percent under the 2020 base, and it has stayed near 57,000 to 58,000 since 2010. Spread over 11.79 square miles, that works out to about 4,937 residents per square mile, so your listing sits among many similar blocks and presentation counts.

Royal Oak Schools teach most children, though a portion of the city's land is zoned to Berkley Public Schools, so confirm your address before listing. Families will ask about the district boundary first.

Rental registration and penalties

A landlord registers with the city before any tenant moves in, and the Building Division then inspects rental units under the Property Maintenance Code. The owner has to name a responsible party within 30 miles, post the address inside the unit, keep within occupancy limits, and maintain working smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and extinguishers.

Short-term rentals add an insurance requirement and a duty to give guests the city's Good Neighbor Policy. Buyers ask for registration paperwork, and an unregistered rental should be fixed before closing. Each repeat violation costs more.

Assessments and tax bills

Summer taxes fall due July 31 and winter taxes February 14. A postmark will not count as proof of payment. A late summer bill accrues interest of one-half of 1 percent a month from August 1, and anything unpaid on March 1 goes to the Oakland County Treasurer. Owners may split the summer bill into two halves, due July 31 and October 31.

Assessed value is set at 50 percent of true cash value, and an inflation multiplier limits taxable value until a transfer happens. Every transferred property gets a review of its deed and affidavit by the Assessor's Office, and that review lifts the cap. For a ballpark new bill, take half the purchase price as taxable value, divide by 1,000 and multiply by the millage rate.

Homestead exemption and appeals

An owner who lived in the home before May 1 of the prior year qualifies for the Principal Residence Exemption, which carries a rate about 15 mills below a non-homestead property. When you sell, rescind your own exemption, and the buyer applies on the new home.

To appeal a value, start with the March Board of Review. Clerical errors and mutual mistakes get corrected at the July and December sessions. Parcel records are free to read on BS&A Online, so look yours over before a buyer does, and note anything that is wrong.

Oakland County recording rules

Staff at the county look over every document before it is recorded, and one defect can cost you weeks. The first page needs a 2.5 inch top margin with half-inch margins on all other sides, and a notary has to sign off on the deed. Older deeds followed different rules: those signed before April 6, 2017 listed the marital status of male grantors, and those signed before March 4, 2002 needed two witnesses.

  • The Sidwell Validation Unit signs off on the legal description before payment is taken.
  • The counter is open weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • Copies are $1 a page, and a certified copy adds $5.
  • Recording runs $30 per deed with the $4 survey surcharge included, and a warranty deed needs a $5 tax certificate from the treasurer.

Transfer tax applies to anything with consideration above $99.99, and the seller pays it under MCL 207.523. The county takes $1.10 per $1,000 and the state takes $7.50 per $1,000.

A cash buyer can often close faster, but the county filing and the assessor's review still apply, and the buyer's taxable value resets after the transfer. Ask for the closing date and net amount in writing from every buyer you talk to.

When the house is a rental

Selling an occupied rental works, as long as the buyer can see the house is registered and inspected. Give over the registration paperwork, the last inspection record and the current lease. After that, ask the Building Division what the new owner files, because a registration gap is easier to fix before closing than after.

If the buyer plans to live in the house, the rental registration question matters less, but the tenant's move-out date and your notice rights still set the closing calendar. Agree on a date in writing so nobody waits on an empty house.

Steps after the closing table

After recording, the Assessor's Office reviews the deed alongside the transfer affidavit and resets the buyer's taxable value. Your Principal Residence Exemption should be rescinded so the lower rate does not follow a house you have sold. Split the summer bill? Confirm the October 31 half is paid or credited at closing. File a copy of the recorded deed and the closing statement with your tax records.

Check the closing statement for the transfer tax lines before you sign. The seller carries the bill, and the amounts follow the shares the county prints.

Must a Royal Oak landlord register before selling?

An occupied rental should already be registered, because registration comes before renting. Give the buyer your paperwork and ask the Building Division what the new owner must file.

What are Royal Oak's tax due dates?

The summer bill is due July 31 and the winter bill February 14. You may pay summer in two halves, with the second due October 31.

How does the homestead exemption change after a sale?

A buyer claims it on the home they are buying, and it cuts the rate about 15 mills compared with non-homestead property. You rescind yours at sale.

What does the county charge to file a Royal Oak deed?

Recording is $30 per deed including the $4 survey surcharge, and the treasurer adds a $5 tax certificate for warranty deeds.

Does taxable value reset when I sell in Royal Oak?

Yes. After the Assessor's Office reviews the deed and affidavit, the cap lifts for the new owner, and the buyer's bill can come out higher than yours.

Selling a house in Kentwood

Kentwood sits in Kent County on the southeast side of Grand Rapids. A sale there follows Michigan's county recording rules, plus a few city offices you deal with directly. The July 2025 population estimate is 54,776, which is 0.8 percent above the 2020 base.

Most sellers start with three questions: what the house might fetch, what the city requires before title moves, and how the tax bill is divided at closing. The sections below answer them in that order, and each one names the Kentwood office that holds the answer.

Home values and rents

For 2020 to 2024, owners are the majority and median rent runs $1,260 a month.

Kentwood Public Schools serves most addresses, while Forest Hills Public Schools and Kelloggsville Public Schools cover parts of the city. Confirm the district for your street before pricing.

Getting the house ready

Kentwood winters are cold, with January highs near 30 degrees Fahrenheit and lows near 15. Buyers' inspectors spend their time on the furnace, attic insulation, roof and basement. If one of those is worn out, either repair it before listing or sell as-is at a price that reflects the work. An as-is cash sale hands that repair risk to the buyer. Whatever route you take, get the furnace serviced and keep the receipt, because heating questions come up first in almost every walkthrough.
