Does a rental house in Kentwood need a certificate before it changes hands?

A rental dwelling in Kentwood must be registered and hold a valid certificate of compliance, and that certificate stays with the owner who earned it. Under the city's rental dwelling inspection ordinance, a certificate can pass to a buyer only if the sale closes within 90 days of the certificate being issued and the buyer tells the city within 30 days of the sale.

Points for a landlord who is selling:

  • A six-year certificate does not transfer. If it moves to a new owner inside the 90-day window it reverts to a two-year certificate.
  • If the buyer never notifies the city, the certificate is suspended, and a replacement is dated back to the sale with fees owed from that date.
  • An owner who lives in a condominium unit needs no registration or certification, but a condominium owned as a rental is treated as a single-family rental.
  • Certificates cannot be issued while the property has unpaid city bills.

Call the Inspections Department at 616-554-0700 before you sign a contract on a rental. Then both sides know the certificate dates and any open violations in advance.

Due dates and appeals

Kentwood mails summer bills in the first week of July, due August 20, and winter bills in the first week of December, due February 14. Unpaid balances move to the Kent County Treasurer on March 1, and a qualifying owner has until September 15 to file a summer deferment with the city.

The assessment side runs on a fixed yearly rhythm:

  • Change notices go out soon after February 1 and carry the appeal dates.
  • The Board of Review begins hearings on the Tuesday after the first Monday in March, by appointment.
  • A homeowner still unhappy after the board has until July 31 to petition the Michigan Tax Tribunal.
  • Occupants claim the school-tax exemption on a homestead by June 1 to cover the summer bill, or November 1 for winter.

An appeal cannot rest on a neighbor's lower tax bill. Michigan lets taxable value rise more slowly for long-term owners, so a recent buyer will usually pay more than an owner next door who has held the house for years.

After the sale: taxable value and your exemption

After the deed records, the buyer owes the Kentwood Assessor a property transfer affidavit within 45 days. Taxable value then resets to the state equalized value for the next tax year, so the buyer's first full bill may look nothing like yours.

You stop claiming your principal residence exemption by filing the rescission form with the city within 90 days of moving out. If you already bought a new Michigan home while the old one sits unsold, you can ask for a conditional rescission, which Kentwood says may run up to three tax years if the house is never rented. The state form is 4640.

Recording the deed

Recording happens downtown in the County Administration Building, 300 Monroe Avenue NW. Two transfer taxes attach to the deed: a state levy of $3.75 per $500 of price, and a county levy that Michigan sets at 55 cents per $500 below 2,000,000 residents. Your title agent should show both on the settlement statement. Ask the title agent who pays the recording costs before you sign.

Some transfers escape the tax, so if your deed is a gift or a correction, ask the title agent whether an exemption applies before money changes hands. Bring a photo ID and your deed information, and expect the register's office to return the recorded deed to the title company after it is processed.

Should you list in Kentwood or take an investor's cash offer?

An investor's cash offer usually closes faster and carries fewer conditions, while a listing reaches more buyers but adds showings and lender timelines. Neither is free of cost, so compare net figures.

Before you sign anything, write down your own requirements: a closing date, the mortgage payoff and a plan for tenants. Ask each buyer in writing who covers recording costs and whether open city violations stay with the house. The Assessor's online sales search shows qualified Kentwood sales, which helps you judge whether an offer sits near the neighborhood's range.

Timing matters too. A cash buyer can often name a closing date within your window, which helps when you are carrying a mortgage payment on a house you have already left. A listing may bring a higher price, but it also adds weeks for showings, a buyer's inspection and a lender's appraisal.

If you plan to list, gather your tax bills, rental certificate if any, and receipts for furnace or roof work. If you plan to sell for cash, those same papers still speed up closing.

Frequently asked questions

What is the median home value in Kentwood?

The median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $268,200. It is a citywide midpoint, so ask for comparables on your own street.

When are Kentwood property taxes due, and where do unpaid taxes go?

The summer bill is due August 20 and the winter bill February 14. Whatever is still open on March 1 goes to the Kent County Treasurer.

What paperwork follows a Kentwood sale?

Mostly the buyer's paperwork: the transfer affidavit goes to the assessor. Your part is the rescission of your principal residence exemption, plus a rental certificate check with Inspections if you were a landlord.

Can I sell a Kentwood rental with tenants still living there?

Yes, but the rental certificate must be valid and the buyer must notify the city within 30 days of the sale for a transferred certificate to stay in force. Call Inspections at 616-554-0700 first.

Which county office records the deed for a Kentwood sale?

The Kent County Register of Deeds, downtown at 300 Monroe Avenue NW. Transfer tax is collected at that recording.

Sell My House Fast in Battle Creek, MI: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Michigan

Sell Your Battle Creek House for Cash

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Battle Creek?
We buy Battle Creek houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Which selling route suits a Battle Creek owner?

A Battle Creek owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer from an investor who accepts the house as it stands. No matter which, the sale ends with a deed recorded in Calhoun County and Michigan transfer tax paid.

Speed and top price rarely arrive together. Listing the house exposes it to the widest group of buyers, yet it depends on a lender's appraisal and an inspection report. A cash sale trades some price for a shorter path, which tends to matter most for a house that is empty, inherited, behind on city code items or full of tenants you would rather not manage.

  • Agent sale: suits sound houses and sellers who can wait months.
  • Private sale: no commission, but you price, show and handle the paperwork.
  • Cash purchase: no repair demands, with a closing day you can often set.

Battle Creek housing and income

Battle Creek lies in the northwest part of Calhoun County, where the Kalamazoo River meets Battle Creek. Roughly two in three households own, and prices run well below Detroit-area levels. Many buyers choose a house by its drive to a large local employer, such as the VA Medical Center, Bronson Battle Creek or Fort Custer Training Center, and I-94 runs through town.

Battle Creek housing and income

Households that own their home (2020-2024)66.0%

The 2025 estimate is 1.4% below the 2020 count of 52,721, so expect a steady market rather than a booming one. Buyers will compare your price with what their monthly payment would be.

Vacant houses and the city ordinance

The vacant-structure ordinance surprises plenty of sellers. When the city identifies a house as empty or abandoned, a registration form goes to the owner of record. It carries a 30-day response window and a $25 fee, and a $40 monthly monitoring charge follows, invoiced quarterly. Unpaid charges from March and September can be added to the property tax bill.

  • If the house is open to entry, you must secure it within 72 hours or the city boards it up and bills you.
  • Vacancy suspends the certificate of occupancy, and more than 24 months revokes it.
  • An owner-occupied house empty 6 to 24 months needs a Property Maintenance Code inspection, and a safety inspection beyond 24 months.
  • A house headed for rental needs registration and an inspection after 2 months or more of vacancy.

Violations follow the address. A buyer gets no extra time to fix problems that existed before the transfer, and that is a common reason mortgage buyers walk away from a neglected house while as-is buyers stay interested.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Battle Creek house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording the deed and paying transfer tax

Deeds are recorded in Marshall, at the Calhoun County Clerk and Register of Deeds in the county building, 315 West Green Street. Staff there cannot coach you through filling out a deed, so a title agent or attorney should prepare it.

The seller owes two taxes under Michigan law. One goes to the state at $3.75 per $500 of value (MCL 207.525). The other goes to the county at 55 cents per $500, since Calhoun has fewer than 2,000,000 residents (MCL 207.504). The combined rate is $4.30 per $500.

The tax is paid to the county treasurer, and the deadline is 15 days after the deed is delivered. Some transfers owe nothing, such as a deed to your child or grandchild, a foreclosure deed and a deed that corrects a flaw in title. Ask the Calhoun County Treasurer whether a tax certification is needed first.

Taxes and the homestead exemption at closing

A lien for summer taxes attaches on July 1, and for winter taxes on December 1. The state default payment dates are September 14 and February 14, but a city charter can set others. Get Battle Creek's exact dates from the City Treasurer and ask the closing office to prorate the bills between you and your buyer.

Owners who live in the house should mail the assessor a Request to Rescind Principal Residence Exemption (Form 2602) inside three months of moving out. Each late day adds $5 until the total hits $200, and the exemption leaves the roll when that calendar year ends. Closing agents commonly hand out the form but carry no legal liability if they forget.

The buyer's math differs from yours. Taxable value stays capped for an owner who remains, but a transfer can lift it to full assessed levels, so the new owner's first bill may exceed what you paid.

Which sellers do well with an all-cash buyer?

Cash makes the most sense when getting ready for a regular listing would cost more than the higher price could repay. Think of a failing roof or furnace, a vacant house piling up monitoring fees, an inherited home whose heirs live elsewhere, or a rental with a difficult tenant history.

Compare offers by what ends up in your pocket. Find out who pays recording and title charges, whether the price can change after a walk-through, and how soon closing can happen. Insist on written terms, and collect a second quote before you sign anything.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Battle Creek houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

A checklist before you sell

  1. Phone Code Compliance and ask whether your address has an open case or a suspended certificate of occupancy.
  2. If the house is empty, find out whether it is already on the vacant-structure list and what has been billed.
  3. If it is a rental, confirm that registration and the city inspection are current.
  4. Get the exact tax due dates from the City Treasurer.
  5. Ask the County Treasurer whether a tax certification is needed on your deed.
  6. Send Form 2602 to the assessor if you lived there.

Run through the list before you accept any offer, and start the week you decide to sell, because some of these calls take time to return. A seller who can show clean paperwork negotiates from a stronger position, whether the buyer is paying cash or arranging a mortgage. A tenant's lease does not end with the sale, so a buyer normally inherits the tenant unless the tenant agrees to leave.

Frequently asked questions

What is a realistic timeline for selling in Battle Creek?

A cash purchase can close within a couple of weeks when title is clear, whereas a listing takes longer because of showings, financing and an appraisal. Liens, probate and open city violations can stretch either path, so check them first.

Does Battle Creek inspect a house before it changes hands?

The city focuses on vacant houses, rentals and addresses with open violations. Phone Code Compliance and ask whether your address has an open case or a suspended certificate of occupancy, since those are what can hold up a sale.

Who is responsible for the state and county transfer tax?

The seller, by statute, though the purchase contract can shift the cost. The rate is $4.30 per $500, and some family transfers qualify for an exemption.

Can a house with tenants be sold in Battle Creek?

Yes. The lease does not end with the sale, so the buyer normally inherits the tenant unless the tenant agrees to leave. For a rental, confirm that registration and the city inspection are current, since a lapse can complicate things.

How soon must I remove my homestead exemption after a sale?

Form 2602 goes to the city assessor, and the clock is 90 days from the move-out. The exemption comes off on December 31 of that year, and each late day adds $5, capped at $200.

Where a Portage sale begins

A Portage sale involves three offices. The city handles permits and property tax bills, the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds records the deed, and the county treasurer supplies the tax certificate that a warranty deed must carry. Listing with an agent or selling straight to a buyer changes none of that. The city's online property records search is updated daily and shows the tax and parcel details a buyer will check first.

Portage is in Kalamazoo County and is the smaller of the two main cities in the Kalamazoo-Portage area. It became a city in 1963. Two lakes in the southeast corner and a tornado in May 2024 are the local details buyers tend to ask about.

Portage housing and population

Portage covers 32.29 square miles of land. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 49,862 residents, a 2.0 percent gain over the April 2020 base of 48,882. Few households move in a given year: 86.8 percent of residents had the same address twelve months earlier.

Lakes and school districts

Buyers who search Portage often start with the water. Austin Lake lies in the southeast part of the city and West Lake sits beside it, with Portage Road running between the two. Houses on or near the lakes are a separate segment from the subdivisions farther north and west.

School district is the other common question, because the city is split. Most of Portage belongs to Portage Public Schools, while smaller areas fall in Comstock Public Schools, Vicksburg Community Schools and Schoolcraft Community Schools. Name the district in your listing. A parcel follows the district boundary, and the city on the mailing address says nothing about it.

Selling a house hit by the May 2024 tornado

The tornado that struck Portage on May 7, 2024 was rated high-end EF2. Reports after the storm counted more than 500 damaged buildings, 60 of them destroyed. The city set up a tornado recovery page for residents and businesses, and the damage path is still the first thing some out-of-town buyers ask about.

If the storm touched your house, put the permits, contractor invoices and insurance paperwork into one folder. Even a buyer paying cash wants to know which roof, siding or windows are new. For a house still waiting on repairs, say so early and weigh selling without repairs against paying for a rebuild. Permits for construction work go through the Portage Department of Community Development, and the Treasury Office collects the permit fees.

The recovery page also lists nonprofit disaster case management for people affected by the storm, which can help with insurance and housing questions while you decide whether to sell. Ask the city manager's office for current contacts, since program details change over time.

Kalamazoo County recording fees

Recording one deed in Kalamazoo County costs a flat $30.00, with another $3.00 for each additional instrument a document assigns or discharges. The office takes cash, check, money order, debit or credit card.

Before recording, a warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract or a master deed must carry the county treasurer's tax certificate. It runs $5.00 for up to 20 tax ID numbers and $0.20 for every description beyond that. A separate $10.00 city certificate applies only to parcels inside the City of Kalamazoo, which excludes Portage.

Transfer tax is figured on the price stated in the deed, rounded up to the next $500 step, at $1.10 per thousand dollars for the county share and $7.50 per thousand dollars for the state share. Michigan's transfer tax act (MCL 207.523) makes the grantor liable, so put that line in your net proceeds estimate and get the exact figure from the title company.

Property tax dates and assessor records

The city collects in two installments. Summer bills open August 1 and are due September 14, and winter bills open December 1 and are due February 14. Each bill covers the full January 1 to December 31 tax year, and a deadline on a weekend rolls to Monday.

  • Balances still open on March 1 pass to the Kalamazoo County Treasury, which adds its own interest and penalties.
  • Special assessments for water, sewer and city street work are billed in July with an August 31 due date, so check for an open installment on the parcel.
  • A lender or escrow agent can request a tax listing from the city after the first bills go out.

For a rough view of the buyer's bill, the State of Michigan Property Tax Estimator lets future owners enter the state equalized value and current owners enter the taxable value. The Portage assessor's office also has a property record form that corrects square footage, bedroom counts and similar facts. Fix any errors before a buyer's appraiser pulls the record.

Selling with tenants in the house

A tenant can stay through closing or move out first, and the lease together with your notice rights sets the timing. Since late 2025 the city has also run a rental listing website for landlords, with free listings for owners of fewer than 20 units. A buyer who plans to keep renting may take over the lease as written, which saves you the search for a new tenant. Ask the Community Development office which local rules apply to your rental, and bring the current lease to every showing.

A short checklist before you list

Print the parcel record from the city's search and check the square footage and bedroom count. Confirm which school district your parcel sits in. Pull permits and receipts for roof, siding, windows and any storm repair. Ask the title company for the transfer tax figure and who covers each recording charge. Then pick the closing date with the tax calendar in mind, so a summer or winter bill is paid or credited cleanly at the table.

What a cash sale skips in Portage

A direct buyer without a loan skips the appraisal, the lender's underwriting and the wait on a financing contingency. That matters most for a storm-damaged or tenant-occupied house, where a lender may balk. The county recording, the tax certificate and the transfer tax still apply, so confirm who pays each one before you sign.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What will recording a Portage deed cost?

A flat $30.00 for the deed at the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds. A warranty deed also needs a treasurer tax certificate at $5.00, which covers up to 20 tax ID numbers.

Does the buyer or the seller owe transfer tax in Portage?

The seller owes it. State law names the grantor, and the county charges $1.10 and $7.50 per thousand dollars for the two shares.

What are the Portage tax deadlines?

September 14 for the summer bill and February 14 for the winter bill. Weekend dates roll to Monday, and open balances pass to the county on March 1.

Can I sell a Portage house damaged in the 2024 tornado?

Yes. Reports counted over 500 damaged buildings after May 7, 2024, and an unrepaired house sells at a price that reflects the work. Keep permits and insurance records for any repairs.

Which district teaches children from my Portage address?

Usually Portage Public Schools, though some parcels belong to Comstock, Vicksburg or Schoolcraft. Confirm with the district before you print it in a listing.

Selling a house in East Lansing

East Lansing is a college town built around Michigan State University, and its rental rules decide who can buy and use your house. The city requires a rental license for most non-owner-occupied homes, some neighborhoods bar new rentals, and many single-family houses carry deed restrictions against renting at all. Those facts change which buyers can pay full price.

The city sits in Ingham and Clinton counties, immediately east of Lansing. Because it spans two counties, the register of deeds and the county treasurer that apply to you depend on the parcel. Ask the East Lansing assessor which county holds your records before you order a title commitment.

East Lansing housing figures

Owned homes here are pricey and renters outnumber owners. The population is young, with a median age of 21.8 at the 2020 census, so houses change hands and tenants more often than in a typical suburb.

With that much movement, an East Lansing listing often meets buyers who plan to rent it out or buy a first home near campus.

Rental license rules that affect value

If your buyer plans to rent the house, the license rules matter as much as the price. The city code lists exceptions where no license is needed, and a seller can help a buyer by knowing them.

  • Family of the owner may live in the house without a license, and two unrelated people count as a family.
  • An owner who is away temporarily may use a house-sitting form for up to two years in a five-year period, but a house that is for sale does not qualify.
  • A seller of a house or duplex may stay up to 90 days after closing under a rental agreement without a license.
  • An estate representative may occupy a house for up to two years from the owner's date of death if the owner lived there for the last year.

Putting a house in an LLC removes the owner-occupancy exception, because an LLC has no family members. A new rental license is not automatic. Some areas have a zoning overlay that prohibits new licenses or limits them to owner-occupied homes. A new application takes a minimum of two months and more often three to four, and a tenant cannot move in before the license is granted.

Neighborhoods and school districts

The city has more than 25 neighborhoods, and many have associations that speak at council and commission meetings. One section is a designated Historic District, and landmark structures in older areas fall under the Historic Preservation Code. Several single-family neighborhoods within a mile of campus have used a petition process under a 2004 zoning ordinance to restrict or prohibit renting.

East Lansing Public Schools reaches most addresses. Portions of the city fall in the Lansing, Okemos, Haslett and Bath districts, so confirm the district on the deed address before you market the house to families.

Property taxes at closing

The city treasury bills both seasons. Summer taxes are levied July 1 and payable without penalty through August 31. Winter taxes are levied December 1 and payable without penalty through February 14 of the following year. Weekend and holiday due dates slide to the next business day, and late payments pick up a 3 percent penalty.

On March 1 each year the city sends unpaid real property taxes to the county, with added interest and penalty. For a payoff after that date, call the Ingham County Treasurer at (517) 676-7220 or the Clinton County Treasurer at (989) 224-5280, depending on where the parcel sits. The city's property tax office, at 410 Abbot Road, takes calls at (517) 319-6826.

State transfer tax and filings

East Lansing sellers owe Michigan's transfer tax, which is $3.75 on each $500 block at the state level (MCL 207.525) with a county layer added (MCL 207.504). Ask the deed office in Ingham or Clinton County for the current county rate. The county treasurer collects it, and the clock is 15 days from handing over the deed.

MCL 207.526 also exempts a quitclaim deed that fixes a flaw in title and an instrument that straightens a boundary line without payment. After closing, the buyer tells the assessor of the transfer within 45 days, and taxable value is reset the following year (MCL 211.27a). Ask the assessor how to rescind your principal residence exemption so the new owner's bill is correct.

Choosing a sale route

A listing aimed at students and landlords depends on the rental license history of the house, so gather license paperwork and any deed restriction notices first. An owner-occupant buyer cares about school district lines and neighborhood overlay rules instead. A direct sale to an investor can work for a house that needs repairs or has a lapsed license, as long as the contract states who handles the license process.

Whichever route you pick, line up the same papers early: your deed details, the latest tax bills, any rental license records and a payoff figure from the right county treasurer. A buyer's agent or closing agent will ask for each of them, and a gap in one tends to slow the whole sale. If the house is a rental with tenants in place, read the lease for its end date and tell the buyer what it says. A buyer who plans to live in the house needs the tenant out, while an investor may want the lease to continue.

Timing a sale around the tax calendar

The tax calendar can make or break a closing date. A sale that closes in July or December lands right as a new bill is levied, so ask the treasury which bill is open and who is expected to pay it. A sale in late summer or midwinter sits close to a penalty date, and a missed deadline adds a 3 percent charge that the closing agent will take from your proceeds.

If taxes have already gone to the county after March 1, the payoff comes from the county treasurer instead of the city. Get the figure in writing and hand it to the closing agent along with your deed information.

Frequently asked questions

Is a rental license part of selling my East Lansing house?

No. Licensing applies to renting, so selling does not need one. A seller of a house or duplex may even stay up to 90 days after closing under a rental agreement without a license, which can help when you need time to move.

Will the next owner of my East Lansing house be allowed to rent it?

Maybe. Many single-family houses carry deed restrictions against renting, some neighborhoods have zoning overlays that bar new licenses, and a license application takes a minimum of two months. Buyers should call the city's Planning, Building and Housing department before closing.

What are the East Lansing tax deadlines?

The summer bill is penalty-free through August 31 and the winter bill through February 14. After those dates a 3 percent charge applies, and real property taxes still unpaid on March 1 are sent to the county.

Which county records my East Lansing deed?

The city spans Ingham and Clinton counties. Deed recording and any delinquent tax payoff go through the county that holds your parcel, so confirm with the city assessor before ordering title work.

Who covers the deed tax at an East Lansing closing?

The seller. The state charges $3.75 on each $500 block and the county adds its own rate. Unless the transfer matches a listed exemption, the county treasurer expects payment within 15 days after the deed changes hands.

Ask the rental division who files the ownership update and when. Give a buyer who plans to keep tenants your most recent Certificate of Compliance. A buyer who plans to move in does not need it, but it helps show the house was inspected and maintained. You can reach the rental division at rentals@roseville-mi.gov, and it can tell you whether your address still needs a registration after the sale.

Assessing forms for buyer and seller

Roseville expects a Property Transfer Affidavit from the buyer within 45 days, and each late day costs $5 up to $200. At closing the buyer also signs the exemption form that saves 18 mills of school operating tax.

Sellers hand in a Request to Rescind Principal Residence at the Assessing Office, which clears the way for an exemption on the next home. From May onward the assessing staff inspect parcels that sold or have active building permits.

The assessor values property at half of its market value. Taxable value can rise each year only by the lesser of inflation and 5 percent, until a sale or physical change resets it. Owners who disagree must appeal by appointment or in writing before the March Board of Review closes.

Macomb County deed filing fees

Macomb charges the same $30 whether a deed runs two pages or twenty, with $3 more per extra instrument a document releases. Four dollars of the $30 goes to a state survey fund.

Before a warranty deed or land contract is accepted, the treasurer stamps a tax certificate, priced at $5 for the first five legal descriptions. The recording office is on North Main Street in Mount Clemens.

On Macomb's schedule the state portion is the price times 0.0075 and the county portion is the price times 0.0011. Sellers are the ones who pay. Conveyances to a child or grandchild and foreclosure transfers are on the county's exemption list, and the deed has to say which exemption applies.

Property tax deadlines and penalties

Bills go out in July and December. Summer payments are due by August 31 and pick up a penalty of 1 percent per month from September 1; winter payments are due by February 28. Anything still open on March 1 is handed to the Macomb County Treasurer.

Homeowners who are 62 or older and earn under $40,000 can postpone the summer bill to February 28 for 1 percent monthly interest, if they file by September 15. Seniors can also get free help with state homestead credits.

A duplicate bill costs $2 a parcel. If you close soon after a due date, ask the title company to confirm payment so the buyer does not inherit a penalty.

Order of events from offer to closing

Start by confirming whether the house is a registered rental. If it is, find the certificate and ask the rental division about the ownership transfer fee. Next, have the title company confirm that summer and winter bills are paid. Sign the deed with the correct exemption language if the transfer qualifies, and send it to Mount Clemens with the tax certificate. Keep the receipt from the recording office, since it is your proof that the transfer was filed. After closing, file the rescission form with Assessing, and remind the buyer about the 45-day affidavit.

Selling a vacant or inherited house

Many Roseville houses are older, and some owners sell after inheriting one or moving out. Empty houses draw attention, so keep the yard tended, the utilities on and the heat set so pipes stay safe. Gather the deed, the latest tax bills and any permits. If the house was rented, find the Certificate of Compliance and any registration record before you call a buyer.

Each buyer should tell you who pays for recording, the tax certificate and the transfer tax. Under Macomb's schedule the seller pays transfer tax, so put it in your net estimate. Compare offers by the amount you would actually keep, not only the price. A buyer who pays cash can often close without waiting on a lender, which helps if a due date is close.

Questions to ask the city and county

Ask the rental division whether your address needs a registration after the sale. Ask the Assessing Office about the principal residence rescission and the 45-day affidavit, since each late day costs $5. Ask the Macomb County treasurer about the tax certificate on a warranty deed. Write down each answer with the date, and hand the notes to your closing agent so nothing is missed. The assessing staff also inspect parcels that sold or have active building permits from May onward, so an unpermitted project is better disclosed than discovered.

If you are 62 or older with a lower income, ask about postponing the summer bill. Free help with state homestead credits is also available for seniors.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a Roseville fee when a rental changes hands?

Yes: $25 for the first unit and $10 for each added unit, on the city's rental fee list.

What does filing a Roseville deed with Macomb County cost?

A flat $30, whatever the page count, with $4 going to the state survey fund. Warranty deeds also need a $5 tax certificate.

Which dates matter for Roseville property tax bills?

August 31 for summer, February 28 for winter, and March 1 when unpaid balances move to the Macomb County Treasurer.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Roseville sale?

The seller, at the 0.0075 state and 0.0011 county multipliers on Macomb's schedule.

How do I end my homestead exemption in Roseville?

File the city's Request to Rescind Principal Residence form with the Assessing Office, then claim the exemption on your next home.

Choosing a sale route in Saginaw

Home values in Saginaw are among the lowest in Michigan, which means the sale route can change your net more than the list price. The middle owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 was $60,000.

Most owners choose one of three paths:

  • An agent listing brings the largest group of buyers, along with showings, inspections and a lender.
  • A private sale saves the commission but puts pricing and paperwork on you.
  • A cash sale as-is suits vacant, tenant-troubled or inherited houses. Gather several offers and read each one's closing terms closely.

City registration rules and county recording steps apply on every route.

Saginaw housing and vacant houses

Saginaw, the county seat, sits on the Saginaw River roughly 15 miles inland from Saginaw Bay. Plant closures changed the numbers: 51,508 residents in 2010, 44,202 in 2020, and an estimate of 42,863 in July 2025. Vacant houses are part of that story. A 2013 federal blight program set aside $11.2 million for Saginaw, and the city began buying unwanted structures for demolition. An empty house of yours needs early attention to grass, boarding and utilities, since neglect cuts value fast.

Saginaw housing and income, 2020 to 2024 estimates

Rent of $922 beside a $60,000 value makes landlord buyers watch repair costs. Receipts for a newer roof or furnace, plus a plain statement of who lives there, help any buyer decide quickly. For pricing, study recent sales on your own street.

Neighborhoods and schools buyers ask about

Saginaw buyers tend to shop by neighborhood first and commute second. Put the neighborhood name in your listing, for example Old Town, Heritage Square, Cathedral District or Sheridan Park, so buyers know what the block is like. Saginaw Public Schools runs the public schools, and Delta College and Saginaw Valley State University are in nearby University Center.

I-75 passes the east side and I-675 loops through downtown. M-13 runs from I-69 through downtown, and M-46 cuts across through Saginaw. Big-box stores and Fashion Square Mall cluster along Bay Road and Tittabawassee Road in Saginaw Township, north of town.

Winter wear on older houses

Expect roughly 49 inches of snow and 32 inches of precipitation yearly, a January mean low of 16.4 degrees Fahrenheit and a record low of minus 23. That kind of cold is hard on roofs, gutters, foundations and furnaces. Inspectors start with the roof, the furnace or boiler, basement moisture and pipes in cold spaces. Disclose any earlier leak, frozen pipe or ice dam at the outset. A repair you explain reads better than one the buyer discovers later.

In a vacant house, keep the heat set low or drain the lines before the cold season. One burst pipe in an empty house can ruin a sellable property within a week.

Rental and vacant house registries

Rented houses and unoccupied houses each have a registry kept by the City Clerk. Ordinance O-275, effective November 27, 2025, dropped the old rule that unpaid taxes or rubbish bills be cleared before a property could register, and the city now collects those amounts another way.

  • Landlords register with the Clerk, and file a current certificate of compliance wherever the code calls for one.
  • Rental registrations expire each year on the fourth Friday of February, and a late renewal adds a 100 percent charge to the base fee.
  • Whoever buys a rental or vacant house has 60 days after title transfers to register it.
  • Owners living in a one-dwelling house, alone or with immediate family, skip registration.
  • An owner who is actively advertising a registered rental for sale or rent does not also have to register it as unoccupied, with a copy of the advertisement as proof.

The unoccupied registry has a 12-month window after purchase for owners who are rehabilitating the house under permit. The Clerk's office, reachable at (989) 759-1480 extension 6, answers registration questions.

Recording and transfer in Saginaw County

The Saginaw County Register of Deeds records deeds for Saginaw property. The fee is $30 per recorded document under MCL 600.2567, with $3 more for each extra instrument a document assigns or discharges. Copies run $1 a page and certification adds $5.

For tax certification, contact the Saginaw County Treasurer. Ask both offices for the state and county transfer tax rates, and for who pays, so the figure appears on your settlement statement in advance.

The buyer reports a change of ownership to the assessor on Form 2766 inside 45 days, under MCL 211.27a(10). Have the closing agent clear property tax bills and city utility balances, so no unpaid amount trails the house to its next owner.

What to line up first

First settle how the house will be shown, whether occupied, vacant or rented. Gather receipts for roof, furnace and plumbing jobs, and list any earlier leak or frozen pipe. Phone the City Clerk if someone besides you has lived there. Then get from each buyer, in writing, a closing date, a net amount and a statement of who pays recording and transfer tax. A cash buyer can skip the wait on a loan, which helps if the house needs work. Compare offers on what you keep after recording, tax certification and any back bills, not only on the headline number. Ask each buyer how soon they can close once title is clear, and whether they will cover any registry fee tied to the transfer.

Documents to hand a Saginaw buyer

A buyer or title company will ask for the deed, the latest tax bill and city utility balances. If the house was a rental, add the registration record and the certificate of compliance. If it was vacant, add anything showing the 12-month rehabilitation window under permit. For repairs you made, supply permits and receipts. A tidy folder tells a buyer the house was looked after, and it speeds up a cash purchase. If a buyer asks for more, send it the same day, because a slow reply can cost you a good offer in a market where buyers have many choices.

Also tell the buyer who lived in the house and when, because the registry rules depend on occupancy. A clear answer prevents a surprise after title transfers.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Saginaw house that needs major repairs?

Yes. Investors and cash buyers regularly take repair-heavy houses as-is. The price will reflect the work, so collect permits, receipts and a list of known problems before requesting offers.

Do I have to register my Saginaw rental before selling it?

If someone other than you lives in the house, it must be on the City Clerk's registry and renewed by the fourth Friday of February. The buyer then registers within 60 days of taking title. Call the Clerk at (989) 759-1480 extension 6 about your case.

What does the county charge to record a Saginaw deed?

$30 per document. Transfer tax and tax certification are separate, so ask the Register of Deeds and the County Treasurer for figures before closing.

Who files the ownership-change form after a Saginaw sale?

The buyer does, on Form 2766 with the local assessor, within 45 days of the transfer. Mention it to your title company as a reminder.

Is Saginaw a hard place to sell a house?

Prices are low, and population dropped from 51,508 in 2010 to an estimated 42,863 in July 2025, so set a realistic price and be patient. Well-documented houses in steady neighborhoods still sell, and a cash sale skips the wait on a loan.

Selling a house in Midland

Midland certifies rentals through its own city program, posts its own tax calendar and records deeds at a flat county fee. Knowing those three items lets a seller schedule a sale without surprises.

Midland is estimated at 42,806 people for 2025, up 0.3% from 2020. Owners live in 67.1% of the 18,535 households, with a median home value of $203,900 and a median rent of $1,048. Median household income is $73,325 and the average commute is 20 minutes.

Midland is the Midland County seat, built where the Chippewa River joins the Tittabawassee, roughly 24 miles northwest of Saginaw and 19 miles west of Bay City. Dow Chemical is the anchor employer, with health care and education following. Midland Public Schools and Bullock Creek Public Schools cover K-12, so confirm the district for your address.

Neighborhoods, utilities and the historic district

The city counts more than 35 neighborhoods, grouped into eight general areas. Downtown includes the Circle business district, Country Club is known for large wooded lots, and the West Main Street Historic District was set up in 1979. Inside the historic district, a commission signs off on construction, additions, repairs, moves and demolitions, so ask it before planning visible work.

City residents get weekly garbage and yard waste pickup and monthly collection of recyclables, large items and brush. Houses in unincorporated areas without municipal water rely on private wells and septic systems, which is worth stating in a listing. Consumers Energy supplies power and gas.

Does the May 2020 flood matter to a Midland buyer?

It often does. Two upstream dams, Edenville and Sanford, failed on May 19, 2020, and about 10,000 Midland residents had to evacuate in what officials called a 500-year flood.

A house that took water, or sits close to either river, sells more smoothly with a paper trail: repair invoices, permits, insurance claims and remediation records. A repaired basement with documents is easier to price than one nobody can account for.

Everyday weather leaves marks too. January highs sit near 29 degrees and snowfall runs 31.4 inches a year, so roofs, gutters and furnaces get a real test each winter.

What Midland requires of a house that has been a rental

Midland inspects and certifies each home, duplex, rooming house, short-term rental and apartment that its owner does not occupy, and the unit may not be rented until certified. That includes houses where no rent is collected and houses occupied by relatives.

A homeowner may keep up to two boarders in a single-family house without an inspection; a third renter triggers one. Four unrelated tenants is the cap for any rental unit. Fees changed on July 1, 2025 to:

  • Rooming house: $105
  • Other rental units: $79 for the first unit and $36 for each extra unit
  • First reinspection per unit: free, with later ones billed at the certification rate
  • Late certification: $36 per unit, with the full certification fee repeated at 30 and at 60 days of delay

The Rental Program takes calls at (989) 837-3383, option 1, or email at rentalprogram@midland-mi.org. Any plan to rent the house for a few months before selling it needs the certificate first.

Tax dates for sellers

Midland mails summer bills on July 1 and winter bills on December 1, and December 31 is Tax Day, the date that fixes the next year's value and classification. The dates stay close to constant from year to year.

Midland tax calendar

A buyer who lives in the house by June 1 qualifies for the summer bill's exemption, and moving in by November 1 covers the winter bill. MCL 211.27a resets taxable value after a sale, so the buyer's first bill will likely differ from yours.

At the Midland County Register of Deeds

Recording costs $30 for any document, however many pages it has. The office sits at 220 W Ellsworth Street and keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5.

  • A warranty deed or land contract needs a $5 certificate proving taxes are current.
  • Transfer tax runs $4.30 per $500 of the sale amount, state and county combined.
  • Copies are $1 a page and a certified copy adds $5.
  • Qualified submitters can e-record, but court orders and death certificates carry a raised seal and go in on paper.
  • The office will not draft a deed or advise on one.

Under MCL 207.526 a deed from parent to child, or grandparent to grandchild, owes no state transfer tax.

Which sale route suits a Midland house?

Match the route to your timeline and the house's condition. A listing works for a sound house with time on the calendar, a private sale for an owner who will do the legwork, and a cash purchase for a house with tenants, flood repairs or a rental certificate still pending.

Give us the Midland address and a rundown of the repairs, and we will quote a price for the house as it stands. Set that figure next to what a listing would net after repairs and fees.

What to gather and what happens next

Before you talk to buyers, collect your deed information, the latest summer and winter tax bills, and any flood repair records. If the house was rented, find the city's rental certificate and note its date. Call the Rental Program before you accept an offer from a buyer who plans to rent. At closing, the title company records the deed for $30, adds the $5 tax certificate for a warranty deed, and collects the transfer tax. Afterward, the buyer files for the principal residence exemption by June 1 or November 1, and you should rescind yours once you move out. A cash purchase skips the lender and the appraisal, so it can close on a date you pick even when repairs or a tenant remain.

If the house sits near the Chippewa or Tittabawassee, expect lenders and buyers to ask about flood history first. Have the repair invoices, permits and insurance claim papers in one folder. A buyer who sees a clean record will often ask fewer questions, and a cash buyer will price the house as it stands whatever the paperwork shows. Either way, the more of the story you can document, the smoother the closing will go for everyone involved.

Frequently asked questions

May I rent my Midland house out while it is for sale?

Only after the city inspects and certifies it. The certification fee is $79 for the first unit, and each late month adds charges.

By what date does a Midland buyer need to claim the principal residence exemption?

The buyer must own and occupy the house by June 1 for the summer bill or November 1 for the winter bill, and files the affidavit with the city.

Who collects Midland taxes that go unpaid?

The Midland County Treasurer. Real property taxes still unpaid on March 1 are turned over to the county.

What is the recording charge for a Midland deed?

$30 per document covers recording. A warranty deed adds a $5 certificate, and transfer tax is billed on the sale price.

Should I mention the 2020 dam failures when I sell a Midland house?

Yes when the property flooded or lies near the Chippewa or Tittabawassee. Keep repair and insurance records handy for questions from buyers and lenders.

The Certificate of Approval requirement

A Lincoln Park seller needs a Certificate of Approval from the city's Building Department before the house can be transferred. The city's ordinance on inspection of residential dwellings prior to sale makes it unlawful to transfer a dwelling, or to act as a broker for the transfer, without a current certificate.

That rule shapes the timeline of every sale in the city, however you find your buyer. The rest of this page explains how the certificate works, then covers the city, its housing figures and the tax and recording steps that follow.

How the inspection process works

The ordinance (Chapter 1488 of the city's codified ordinances) requires anyone about to transfer a dwelling to register with the Building Department so an inspection can be scheduled. City Council sets the fee by resolution, so ask the department for the current amount.

Main points of the chapter:

  • A Certificate of Approval is valid for one sale or transfer, and a new inspection is required each time the dwelling is sold again.
  • A dwelling includes the house and accessory uses such as garages, sheds, pools, gazebos and playhouses.
  • A buyer may take responsibility for correcting violations by signing a notarized affidavit filed with the Building Department. If the violations are not corrected within six months, occupancy may be prohibited.
  • Failing to obtain the certificate is a municipal civil infraction with a $500 fine.

Inspectors may enter during normal business hours, and owners, agents and occupants must give access to every part of the property they control. The enforcing official can also order immediate action to remove a hazard. Clear access to the garage, sheds and any pool or gazebo before the inspection date, because accessory structures are part of what the ordinance covers.

A transfer means a sale, a land contract or the exercise of an option to purchase. Gifts, devises and lien foreclosures are outside the definition. Rentals follow a separate track, covered next.

Certificates for owner-occupied and rental houses

Lincoln Park uses different certificates for different situations, and sellers sometimes confuse them. Three are named in the ordinance.

Certificates under Lincoln Park Chapter 1488
CertificateApplies toHow long it lasts
Certificate of ApprovalResidential dwelling being sold or transferredOne sale or transfer
Certificate of ComplianceRental dwellings and rental unitsThree years, unless the property is sold first
Certificate of OccupancyApproved use or occupancy under the zoning ordinancesIssued by the Building Department

A rental that holds a current Certificate of Compliance is not treated as a dwelling for the Certificate of Approval rule, but a new inspection and a new Certificate of Compliance are required before a rental is sold or transferred. If you own a rental, schedule that inspection before you sign a contract.

Lincoln Park and its housing market

Lincoln Park is a Downriver suburb of Detroit in Wayne County, about 11 miles southwest of downtown. It packs 38,529 residents (July 2025 estimate, down 4.3 percent from the 2020 base) into 5.84 square miles, and its neighbors include Detroit, Allen Park, Melvindale, Ecorse, Wyandotte and Southgate. Lincoln Park Public Schools serves residents.

Figures for 2020 to 2024:

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $131,000
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 68.8%, with 14,767 households
  • Median gross rent: $1,023
  • Median monthly owner costs: $1,169 with a mortgage, $530 without
  • Same house one year ago: 91.3%
  • Persons per household: 2.66

At a median near $131,000, a five-figure repair matters a great deal to a seller's net. Price the house with the inspection list in hand, since a buyer will do the same.

When are Lincoln Park property taxes due?

The city treasurer collects only current-year taxes. Summer bills are mailed by the end of June and fall due August 20, with later installment dates for owners who pay in parts, and a 1 percent penalty applies on the 20th of each month to unpaid summer taxes. Winter bills are mailed around the end of November and are due in mid-February, with a 1 percent monthly penalty after that.

All unpaid taxes transfer to the Wayne County Treasurer on March 1. Online payments carry a 2.95 percent processor charge, and a duplicate bill costs $10 unless you print the record from the city site. Title companies, agents and landlords are told this in a notice on the city's tax page.

Business personal property is taxed through the same office. Anyone operating on December 31 owes the following year's entire billing cycle, under state law.

Deed recording and transfer tax

Lincoln Park deeds are recorded by the Wayne County Register of Deeds. The Wayne County Treasurer must certify taxes on a deed first in most cases, and visits are by appointment. The fee schedule that began January 1, 2026 sets a deed at $26, with a $4 survey fee where it applies.

The state tax comes to $3.75 per $500 of price, with a separate county tax. State law exempts some conveyances, for example a deed given in foreclosure and a land contract that has not yet passed title, so ask the title company whether yours qualifies.

Afterward, the buyer sends the assessor a transfer affidavit within 45 days, and your own homestead exemption should be cancelled within 90 days of your move.

Putting it together: a seller's checklist

Start with the Building Department, because the inspection sets your schedule. Register, book the inspection, and clear the garage, sheds and any pool or gazebo. Read the inspector's findings and decide whether to fix each item or let the buyer sign the notarized affidavit. Pull your current tax bills, since only current-year taxes are paid at the city and anything unpaid after March 1 sits with the county. At closing, ask the title company to show the state transfer tax and the county tax on the settlement statement.

A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can handle the Certificate of Approval steps and the affidavit on their side, which saves you the repair work. Owners of rentals should have a current Certificate of Compliance or schedule a new inspection before signing any contract.

Remember the order of operations when a buyer takes on violations. The affidavit goes to the Building Department, the six-month clock starts, and occupancy can be prohibited if the work is not finished. A buyer who plans to move in right away should price that work into the offer, and a seller can use the inspector's list as the basis for negotiating. Keep a copy of every document you sign.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an inspection to sell my house in Lincoln Park?

Yes. Lincoln Park requires a Certificate of Approval from the Building Department before a dwelling is transferred, and a new one for every sale. Register with the department so it can schedule the inspection, and ask what the council-set fee is.

What is the fine for selling without a Certificate of Approval?

The ordinance sets the fine at $500, as a municipal civil infraction. It also states that other statutory and common-law rights and actions are not limited by that penalty, so a buyer or the city may have further remedies.

Can a buyer take over the violations in Lincoln Park?

Yes, by signing a notarized affidavit that states the buyer's intent to correct them and filing it with the Building Department. If the violations are not corrected within six months, occupancy may be prohibited, so a buyer needs a realistic repair budget and schedule.

What is a Lincoln Park house worth?

The median owner-occupied home value is $131,000 for 2020 to 2024, and median gross rent is $1,023.

When do unpaid Lincoln Park taxes go to the county?

On March 1, everything unpaid belongs to the county treasurer, and the city no longer takes those payments.

Sell My House Fast in Muskegon, MI: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Michigan

Selling in Muskegon?

What a Muskegon seller should expect

Muskegon sellers deal with a city that registers and inspects every rental, a lake-effect climate that is hard on roofs, and a county office that records deeds for a flat fee. A house that was ever a rental carries the most paperwork.

The 2025 estimate puts the city at 37,224 people, level with its 2020 base. Of 13,996 households, 53.1% own their home. Owned homes are valued at $142,300 at the median, rent is $996, and owners with a mortgage pay a median of $1,064 a month. At those prices, a repair bill of a few thousand dollars takes a big bite out of a sale.

Where Muskegon sits and what buyers like

Muskegon is the Muskegon County seat, a harbor city on the south shore of Muskegon Lake with Lake Michigan just beyond. Neighbors include North Muskegon, Muskegon Township, Fruitport Township, Muskegon Heights, Roosevelt Park and Norton Shores, and Grand Rapids lies 42 miles to the southeast.

The waterfront is a draw. Downtown has about two miles of lakefront, a convention center completed in 2021 and the Trinity Health Arena. I-96, US 31, M-46 and M-120 serve the city, MATS runs buses and trolleys, and Muskegon County Airport has nonstop service to Chicago O'Hare. Muskegon Public Schools serves the city, so confirm the district for your address.

Snow and your roof

Snow is the main wear factor. A year brings 87.2 inches, with January alone at 29.1 inches, and 48 days with measurable snow, mostly lake-effect. Roofs, gutters and furnaces take that punishment, and an inspector on the buyer's side will start there. Keep invoices for any roof, gutter or basement work, and service the furnace before showings.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Muskegon house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Rental rules that follow a house into a sale

Every rental in the city must be registered and inspected, and the certificate stays with the owner who earned it. Anyone buying with a rental plan starts fresh, with a new certificate and a new inspection.

A clean first inspection earns a 6-year certificate, while violations put the property on a 3-year cycle. Because the city works under the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code, rentals need carbon monoxide readers, and a contractor must certify the furnace and water heater at 0 ppm in the breathable area. An owner who lives more than 30 miles off must name a responsible party within 30 miles.

The first reinspection costs $50 per unit and each later one adds $20. A lockout, late cancellation or no-show runs $70 per unit.

Does a Muskegon short-term rental license go with the house?

Usually not. Licenses issued after the ordinance was adopted cannot be transferred, so the registration stays with the owner who obtained it.

One exception exists for properties with an active short-term rental status before March 2024. They may make a one-time status transfer in any zone using a signed formal document, and the new owner still completes registration and inspections. The overlay district has 11 zones with caps ranging from 13 in Zone 11 to 95 in Zone 9, and Zone 1, Beachwood and Bluffton, is full with a waitlist. Properties inside the downtown authority, the Lakeside Business Improvement District and the Lakeside Corridor Improvement Authority fall outside the caps.

A single-family short-term rental pays $500 a year, with each added unit adding another $500. Any buyer whose offer rests on vacation-rental income should read the overlay rules before signing.

Tax deadlines at closing

The city bills in two rounds. Summer bills issue July 1 and are due September 14, and winter bills issue December 1 and are due February 14.

Summer taxes left unpaid collect 1% interest monthly once past due and a 3% penalty if still open on February 14, while winter taxes take a 3% penalty after their due date. Whatever the city has not collected by February 28 becomes delinquent on March 1 and the County Treasurer collects it. Your title company will prorate the current bill at the closing table.

The buyer's taxable value is reset the year after the sale (MCL 211.27a), which can lift the next bill well above yours. If you claimed the principal residence exemption, rescind it within 90 days of moving out or face $5 a day, up to $200 (MCL 211.7cc).

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Muskegon houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Recording costs at the Muskegon County Register of Deeds

One flat charge applies: $30 per deed, mortgage or other instrument, however many pages.

  • Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments with a warranty clause first need a $5 certificate from the County Treasurer's Office.
  • Real estate record copies run $1 a page, plus $5 per certification.
  • Combined transfer tax is $4.30 per $500 of price.
  • A free Fraud Guard alert emails you whenever your name appears on a recorded document.

Gifts between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild are exempt from state transfer tax (MCL 207.526).

How should I choose a way to sell in Muskegon?

The choices are a listing, a sale by owner or a cash purchase. Weigh repair costs, carrying costs and timing against price, because a lower-priced house can lose a bigger share of its value to fixes.

Before you talk to buyers, gather:

  • The rental certificate and latest furnace and water heater inspection, if the house was rented
  • The latest summer and winter tax bills, so the closing agent can settle what is owed
  • Records of roof, gutter and basement work after a lake-effect winter
  • Your deed or land contract paperwork

For a cash price, send us the Muskegon address and the house's condition. We buy as-is, so a failed rental inspection or a winter-damaged roof need not be fixed first.

From offer to closing day

Once you have a buyer, the sequence is short. The title company checks the deed, asks the County Treasurer's Office for the $5 certificate if the deed carries a warranty, and prorates the current tax bill. You sign the deed, and the Register of Deeds records it for $30. If your name is signed on a recorded document, the free Fraud Guard alert tells you by email, which is a handy way to confirm the recording happened.

Afterward, rescind your principal residence exemption within 90 days of moving out. If the house was a rental, remember that the certificate does not move with it, so the buyer opens a new one. A cash purchase skips the lender and the appraisal, and it lets you leave a rental with tenants or a failed inspection behind without fixing anything first.

Frequently asked questions

Will my Muskegon rental certificate pass to the buyer?

No. Rental certificates do not transfer to new owners, so a buyer opens a new certificate, passes an inspection and pays the registration fee. Mention that early if your buyer plans to rent the house out.

How long does a Muskegon rental certificate last?

Six years after a clean first inspection and three years when violations are found. The yearly registration fee keeps it in good standing between inspections.

When do unpaid Muskegon taxes go to the county?

March 1. The city passes along anything uncollected by February 28, and the County Treasurer takes over from there.

What transfer tax does a Muskegon seller owe?

Combined state and county transfer tax is $4.30 per $500 of price. Gifts between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild are exempt from state tax.

What does a Muskegon short-term rental registration cost?

$500 a year for a single-family unit, rising to $1,000 for a duplex and $2,500 for a quinplex. Reinspections start at $100 and climb in $100 steps.

Selling in Holland?

Why Holland's county line matters to a seller

Holland straddles a county line, and that touches nearly every step. Thirty-second Street divides the city between Ottawa County on the north and Allegan County on the south, so the deed, the treasurer and the school district can all depend on which side your house stands. Whether the house is listed, sold privately or bought for cash, first confirm which county holds your parcel.

The city sits beside Lake Macatawa, about 5 miles east of Lake Michigan, and its 17.45 square miles split into 9.08 on the Ottawa side and 8.13 on the Allegan side. Mid-2025 estimates put the population at 35,372, up 2.9 percent from the 2020 base.

Older homes and local demand

A fire on October 8 to 10, 1871 burned most of downtown, which is why older homes gather in the Historic District and around it. Neighborhoods people mention include Holland Heights, Westside, Washington Square, Hope, Maplewood, South End and Downtown.

Jobs come from manufacturing, tourism, agriculture and higher education, with Hope College and a Grand Valley State University campus in town. The Tulip Time festival each May brings visitors who book local homes, so the short-term rental rules below include a festival category.

Holland prices and ownership

Survey estimates for 2020 through 2024:

  • Typical owner-occupied home: $252,200.
  • Homeownership: 67.8 percent of 12,977 households.
  • Typical rent: $1,193.
  • Persons per household: 2.34.
  • Average trip to work: 16.8 minutes.

Short commutes and a mix of furniture and automotive employers support demand, yet a house needing a roof, furnace or foundation work still sells below the typical price. A cash buyer pricing a repair-heavy house starts from the repaired value and subtracts the work.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Holland house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Which offices and schools serve my house?

Nearly all of the Ottawa County side lies inside Holland Public Schools. On the Allegan side, Holland Public Schools covers most of the area and Hamilton Community Schools the remainder. The city's own millage table reflects this with a separate Hamilton line.

Each deed goes to the register of deeds for its own county. Ottawa County records at its office on Fillmore Street in West Olive and offers a web portal for one-off e-recording, while Allegan County's register handles the southern side. Overdue taxes are a county matter, handled by the Ottawa or Allegan treasurer. The current bill itself comes from the city treasurer.

Tax bills, deadlines and millage

The city dates the summer bill July 1 and sets the payment deadline in mid-August. The winter bill follows on December 1. The city adds a 1 percent administration fee to both bills. Qualifying seniors and disabled homestead owners may ask to defer the summer payment, which moves the due date to mid-February.

The 18-mill gap between the two columns is the school operating tax that a homeowner's exemption removes, so an investor who will not occupy the home pays the higher rate.

Rentals and short-term stays

Chapter 14 of Holland's ordinance code governs rentals, which matters if tenants live in the house you are selling. Each unit must be registered, and the annual fee carries a December 10 deadline. An unregistered rental or unreported change draws a $200 late fee, and an unpaid annual fee is a misdemeanor. Inspections come every 3 or 6 years, and a passing unit earns a Certificate of Compliance.

Short-term stays follow a separate track, and the city sorts them into three types:

  • Owner-occupied: your own primary residence, permitted in every zone.
  • Investor-owned: a home the owner does not live in. Permitted in mixed-use, industrial and similar districts, and in residential districts only within a cap of 25 properties and a 500-foot spacing rule. Ask the city whether any slots remain.
  • Tulip Time: a home offered no more than 10 days during the May festival, with no inspection or certificate required.

A buyer planning an investor-owned short-term rental in a residential zone should confirm capacity with the city first.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Holland houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How the transfer tax works

Sellers pay it. Michigan's state rate is $3.75 per $500 of price (MCL 207.525), and a county with under 2,000,000 residents adds 55 cents per $500 (MCL 207.504). Payment goes to the county treasurer inside 15 days after the deed is delivered.

MCL 207.526 exempts gifts to a child or grandchild, court-ordered transfers with no set price, and deeds from foreclosed government-backed loans. If your lot touches 32nd Street, ask the register in each county how the parcel is recorded.

Exemptions that end or start at closing

Your principal residence exemption changes at closing. State law (MCL 211.7cc) has the owner file a rescission no later than 90 days after the house stops serving as a principal residence. A newcomer who moves in files an affidavit, due June 1 for the summer levy and November 1 for the winter levy. Holland's assessing office handles both forms.

Other relief exists as well: a home repair exemption under Public Act 25 of 1978 that holds assessed value steady up to the sale, a hardship exemption (MCL 211.7u), and relief for disabled-veteran owners. If you used any of them, tell the buyer, because the first bill after closing may look different.

Lake Macatawa and basements

Homes near Lake Macatawa and the Macatawa River sit at about 610 feet of elevation, so expect your buyer's inspector to check basements for moisture. Fix gutters or grading before showings, and keep the furnace in good order, since a winter failure can freeze pipes.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

A short order of steps for sellers

Begin by finding your parcel's county, then ask that county's register how the deed will be recorded and ask the right treasurer for any overdue balance. Confirm with the city whether your house is a registered rental or has a short-term rental permit, and gather the certificate if so. Ask the assessing office about any exemption you hold, such as the principal residence exemption, so the rescission goes in on time.

Then compare offers by what you keep after the transfer tax and the tax proration. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands saves you the roof, furnace or grading work, but get the closing date and proof of funds in writing before you accept.

Frequently asked questions

In which county is my Holland deed recorded?

The one that holds your parcel. Holland spans Ottawa County (north) and Allegan County (south) with 32nd Street as the boundary, and each keeps its own register of deeds.

When is the City of Holland summer tax due?

Mid-August. The bill is dated July 1, and a 1 percent administration fee is added to the summer and winter bills.

What happens to my Holland rental registration when I sell?

Registration and certification belong to the rental operation, and the city wants ownership changes reported. A missed report costs a $200 late fee, so tell the city about the sale.

Can my buyer operate a short-term rental in Holland?

Owner-occupied ones are allowed in every zone. Investor-owned ones in residential districts are limited to 25 properties with 500 feet of spacing, so check capacity first.

Who pays the transfer tax on a Holland sale?

The seller, at $3.75 per $500 of price for the state plus 55 cents per $500 for the county. Family transfers to a child or grandchild are exempt.

Selling a house in Eastpointe

Eastpointe is a small, dense Macomb County city of 5.16 square miles. Most of what sellers deal with is rental registration, tax billing and school boundaries rather than a pre-sale inspection. Owners live in about seven of every ten homes, so many buyers are families looking for a first or second home.

The city peaked at 45,920 residents in 1970, slipped to 32,442 by 2010 and has hovered near 34,000 since. Downtown Detroit is ten miles southwest, and 8 Mile Road forms the southern edge of the city.

Eastpointe housing figures

Rents are high against modest home values, so rented houses are common here and the city's rental registration rules come up in many sales.

Rental and vacant property rules

The Building Department manages registration and inspection of every non-owner-occupied residential property, and tenants cannot occupy a rental until the city certifies it. If your house is rented, the buyer inherits that regime.

  • Rentals must be registered and inspected every two years from the application date.
  • If a property is certified at the time of sale, the certificate may transfer to the new owner when that owner registers within 14 days of purchase.
  • Owners and property managers complete a one-time registration separate from the property registration.
  • An owner who lives 50 miles or more from city hall must name a local agent.
  • A furnace or boiler must pass an inspection by a qualified contractor.

Vacant buildings have their own rule: register inside 45 days of the vacancy, renew each year until the property is occupied again, and obtain a certificate of compliance for re-occupancy. Call the Building Department at 586-445-3661 for rentals (extension 2269) or vacant properties (extension 2214).

School districts and roads

Eastpointe Community Schools reaches most parcels. South Lake Schools claims the southeastern corner, and its Koepsell Elementary stands inside Eastpointe's borders. Confirm the district for your parcel before listing, since boundaries shape what a family will pay.

Gratiot Avenue (M-3) runs through the city, with I-94 and I-696 close by, and 8 Mile Road (M-102) and 9 Mile Road carry cross-town traffic. Commuters like that access, and it is worth mentioning in a listing.

Due dates and penalties

The City Treasurer collects for the city, Macomb County, Macomb Community College, the intermediate school district, the state education tax and both school districts. About 30,000 bills go out each year, and both school districts ask that 100 percent of school tax appear on the summer bill.

  • Summer taxes are due July 1 with a September 1 deadline. Pay it all by September 1, or pay half by then and the other half by December 1.
  • Winter taxes are due December 1 with a February 15 deadline.
  • A summer balance left after September 1 grows by 1 percent a month, with 2 percent more from February 16.
  • A winter balance left after February 15 carries a 3 percent charge.
  • From March 1, unpaid taxes go to the Macomb County Treasurer at One South Main Street in Mount Clemens, with added penalties.

Eligible owners can defer summer taxes to February 15 if household income is $40,000 or less and they are 62 or older, disabled, a qualifying veteran, a surviving spouse or blind. The deferment application is due by September 15. For a payoff figure, call the taxes line at 586-445-3661, option 6.

Assessor paperwork after a sale

The buyer signs the principal residence exemption form at closing if the house will be owner-occupied. The seller signs a request to rescind the exemption and files it with the assessor, which clears the seller's name from the homestead and lets the seller claim it on the next home.

Buyers owe the assessor a Property Transfer Affidavit, due 45 days after the transfer. Each late day costs $5, capped at $200. The taxable value is uncapped the year after a transfer, so the new owner's bill rises to match the assessed value, which the city sets at half of market value.

An owner who thinks the value is too high must appear in March, since that is the only month the Board of Review hears opinions of value. The July and December sessions deal with clerical errors, mutual mistakes of fact and hardship requests. A homeowner who loses can take the case to the Michigan Tax Tribunal by June 30.

State transfer tax

On an Eastpointe sale the seller pays the state transfer tax, $3.75 on each $500 block of value (MCL 207.525). Macomb County adds a levy of its own under MCL 207.504. The county deed office at 586-469-7953 can tell you the current total, and the county treasurer collects it, with a 15-day deadline that starts when the deed is delivered.

MCL 207.526 exempts, among others, a deed that does nothing but straighten a boundary line and a land contract that has not yet passed legal title. A land contract buyer can still claim the principal residence exemption if the contract is recorded or recordable.

What a seller should do first

Start by finding out whether the house is owner-occupied or rented. If it is rented, call the Building Department and ask whether the rental certificate is current and whether it can pass to a buyer who registers inside the 14-day window. Then call the taxes line for a payoff figure, and confirm which school district serves the parcel. With those three answers you can list the house, or talk to a cash buyer, knowing what the buyer will inherit and what the closing agent has to pay from your proceeds.

What a buyer will ask you for

Expect a buyer's agent or lender to ask for the rental certificate if the house is a tenant-occupied property, proof that any vacant-building registration is current, and a clear tax payoff. Owner-occupant buyers will also want to know which school district serves the house. Have these papers ready before showings begin, and the offers you get will be based on facts instead of guesses. If a payoff shows a balance after March 1, the Macomb County Treasurer holds it, so allow time for that office to answer before your closing date.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a pre-sale inspection for an Eastpointe house?

The city's rules cover rental registration and vacant property registration, not a general pre-sale inspection. If the house is a rental, the certificate may pass to the buyer if the buyer registers within 14 days. Call the Building Department to confirm your property's status.

When are Eastpointe summer and winter taxes due?

Summer bills are issued July 1 with a September 1 deadline, and winter bills December 1 with a February 15 deadline. Whatever is unpaid on March 1 goes to the Macomb County Treasurer.

How do I remove my principal residence exemption after selling?

Sign a request to rescind the exemption and file it with the Eastpointe Assessing Department. That clears your name from the homestead so you can claim the exemption on your next home.

What does the buyer file after an Eastpointe closing?

A Property Transfer Affidavit, filed at the Assessor's Office. The closing agent usually supplies the form, but the buyer must file it, and a filing later than 45 days costs $5 per day up to $200.

Which district serves an Eastpointe address?

Eastpointe Community Schools covers most parcels, while the southeastern corner belongs to South Lake Schools. Look up your parcel before you list.
