Which sale method fits a Bay City house?

A Bay City seller can list on the open market, run the sale personally, or accept a cash purchase from someone who takes the property in its present condition. All three finish with a recorded deed and Michigan transfer tax, so the real decision is how much time, repair work and uncertainty you want to carry.

An older house near the river often needs the most thought. Many Bay City homes date from the lumber era, and a buyer using a mortgage will usually order an inspection that turns up wiring, roofing or foundation items. A cash buyer prices those in and skips the repair negotiation.

  • Listing: the broadest audience and the longest wait, with repair requests likely.
  • Owner-run sale: no listing commission, yet you handle contract and disclosures.
  • Cash purchase: a simpler closing, with the price tied to the house's condition.

Bay City homes and prices

Bay City is the Bay County seat, on the Saginaw River just upstream from Saginaw Bay. West Bay City, on the river's west bank, was a separate city until it was annexed in 1905, and several bridges still link the two sides. The Center Avenue Historic District holds more than 250 buildings on the National Register, many of them lumber-boom houses, and waterfront and historic-district homes draw a particular kind of buyer. Bay City Public Schools runs three high schools, Central, Western and Eastern, so list the attendance zone clearly.

Values sit below $100,000 at the median, and the population has been slipping since 2010.

Industrial pockets along Morton Street, Harrison Street and Woodside Avenue sit close to some of the older housing, which can affect noise and traffic for a buyer.

Bay City rental rules

The city requires every rental property to be registered, inspected and certified before a tenant occupies it, and its rental page carries the registration forms and a tenant complaint form. A rental that was never registered can come to light when a code officer visits, and that is better dealt with before a buyer's inspector finds it.

For a rental sale, pull together the registration, the certificate and any correction letters from past inspections. An investor taking over the tenants will ask for them, and an owner-occupant will want proof that every unit is legal.

Utilities add one local wrinkle. Bay City runs its own utility billing, and trash charges are placed on electric accounts for occupied and unoccupied homes alike. Settle the final bills and ask Utility Customer Service at 989-894-8104 about closing out the accounts at the transfer.

Bay County Register of Deeds charges

The Register of Deeds takes a flat $30 for each deed, mortgage or other instrument, however many pages it runs, and $4 of that goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund. A warranty deed, land contract or condominium master deed also needs a tax certificate from the Bay County Treasurer, priced at $5 on its own check.

Two statutes produce the transfer tax. The county's posted schedule shows $7.50 for the state and $1.10 for the county on each thousand dollars of consideration, which makes $8.60 per thousand. The seller pays it.

Either the deed states the full price or an affidavit accompanies it, and a claimed exemption must be noted in the instrument itself. The state act exempts, for example, a gift deed to your child and a deed given in foreclosure.

Property taxes when you sell

From March 1, any unpaid residential tax is payable to the Bay County Treasurer at 515 Center Avenue (989-895-4285), where interest and fees build. Have the title company verify that summer and winter bills are settled or prorated before recording.

The state's default summer deadline is September 14, yet a charter can move it, so confirm Bay City's date with the Treasurer. Under the state schedule a late summer payment gains 1% a month, and whatever remains unpaid goes back to the county on March 1.

Anyone who claimed a principal residence exemption should send the rescind form to the city assessor within 90 days of leaving. The assessor can supply the form.

Cash offer or listing: figuring your net

The honest comparison is between two totals, not two headline prices. A listing can bring a higher number, but the deductions add up and the wait has its own cost. A cash offer is usually lower and more predictable. Write both columns down on one sheet of paper, then decide which one fits your timeline.

Estimate your net on each path. On a listing, take away agent fees, repairs the buyer's inspection will request, transfer tax and the cost of carrying the house while you wait. On a cash offer, take away only what the buyer says you will pay, and have that stated in writing.

Ask each buyer who covers title and recording, whether the offer can shift after a walk-through, and which closing date is firm. A buyer worth dealing with answers plainly and lets you take time to compare.

Steps before you close

  1. Decide whether the house will be listed, sold privately or sold for cash.
  2. If tenants live there, gather the registration, certificate and inspection letters.
  3. Ask the Treasurer at 989-895-4285 about the status of summer and winter bills.
  4. Arrange the tax certificate for a warranty deed, which costs $5 on its own check.
  5. Settle utility accounts through Utility Customer Service at 989-894-8104.
  6. Send the rescind form to the assessor if you claimed a principal residence exemption.

If the house needs real repairs, get one or two contractor estimates before you decide. A figure you can quote makes it easier to judge a cash offer that already accounts for the work, and it shows a retail buyer you are not hiding anything. Disclose known defects either way.

Your title company usually submits the deed right after closing. Ask them for the recording confirmation date, and keep it with your closing papers.

Frequently asked questions

Is a Bay City house with big repair needs still sellable?

Yes. An as-is buyer folds the repairs into the offer, and you can alternatively list at a lower price while disclosing known defects. Set the repair estimate beside the $97,600 middle home value in Bay City before you spend on renovation.

What transfer tax does a Bay City sale carry?

State tax of $7.50 and county tax of $1.10 per $1,000 combine to $8.60. The seller pays it unless the contract assigns it elsewhere.

Must a Bay City rental be registered before I sell?

The city requires registration, inspection and certification before any tenant moves in. If your house has been rented, collect the paperwork early, since buyers and title companies may request it.

Where do overdue Bay City taxes go after March 1?

They are payable to the Bay County Treasurer from that date. Clear the balance with the county or through the closing so the buyer receives clean title.

When does the Bay County deed get recorded?

The Register of Deeds records documents that meet its requirements and returns any that do not. Your title company normally submits the deed right after closing, so ask them for the recording confirmation date.

Selling a house in Jackson

Jackson is the seat of Jackson County, so a sale here passes through two sets of offices. City hall on West Michigan Avenue deals with assessing, treasury and rental registration, while the county records the deed. Whether you list with an agent, find a buyer yourself or accept an as-is cash offer, closing follows the same legal steps. The real differences are the shape the house is in and who lives there.

Jackson sits at the junction of I-94 and US 127, roughly 35 miles west of Ann Arbor, 35 miles south of Lansing, 75 miles west of Detroit and 65 miles east of Kalamazoo. The mid-2025 population estimate is 31,022, a 0.9 percent slip from the 2020 base.

What Jackson homes sell for

Survey figures for 2020 through 2024 show a low-cost market:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $103,200.
  • Homeownership: 54.7 percent of 13,281 households.
  • Typical rent: $898 a month.
  • Average trip to work: 17.0 minutes.

With a typical value near $103,000 and almost half of households renting, many Jackson houses belong to investors or need repairs. Expect buyers to inspect the roof, furnace and foundation closely. Winters are cold, with a January low averaging 17.5 degrees and about 37.3 inches of snow a year, so a sound furnace and roof are real selling points. If repair costs would run higher than what they add to the price, an as-is sale to a cash buyer may be the simpler path.

Rental registration after a sale

Jackson keeps a registry of rentals that are not owner-occupied, and a sale restarts it. A registration is good for 3 years, owners report changes within 10 days, and renewals are due no later than 60 days before expiry. Selling voids the registration, and the new owner applies at closing. Within 45 days after the sale, the seller of a rented dwelling tells the Community Development Department who bought it and where to reach them.

A buyer who claims a 100 percent principal residence exemption with the city assessor skips registration. Anyone else registers within 45 days of closing, with a $5 per unit daily penalty for lateness. Fees are not refunded or credited on a transfer, so a seller who just paid for a registration cannot recover it.

If you own a rental, tell your buyer about the registration rules before the offer is final. An investor who plans to keep the tenants needs to know the paperwork starts over on their side.

Due dates and the assessing calendar

City bills arrive July 1 (summer) and December 1 (winter). Pay the summer bill in one lump by July 31, or split it into five payments due on the 20th from July to November. The winter bill is open for payment December 1 to February 14. The assessor's calendar sets the rest of the year:

Jackson assessing calendar for a property owner
DateWhat happens
February 14Final penalty-free day for last year's winter bill
Second week of MarchAssessment appeals heard by the Board of Review
June 1Principal residence exemption claims due
July 31Summer bill due; last day for a residential Tax Tribunal appeal following a March Board of Review appeal
December 31Tax day: condition of the property on this date sets the next assessment

Ask the treasurer's office for a payoff figure before closing so your title company can settle whatever is still open.

Why will a buyer's Jackson tax bill likely exceed mine?

Taxable value on a Michigan home can climb only by the lesser of 5 percent or inflation each year while one owner holds it. A sale ends that cap. Under MCL 211.27a, the next calendar year's taxable value jumps to the state equalized value, roughly half of market value. Someone who has owned for decades pays far less than the person who buys from them, so tell serious buyers early while they are still comparing monthly costs.

You also have a form to file. Once you move out, rescind your principal residence exemption within 90 days (MCL 211.7cc) and send it to the Jackson assessor.

City income tax after you sell

Jackson levies its own income tax. Residents with income over $600 file and pay 1 percent. People who commute in to work pay 0.5 percent, and corporations and partnerships pay 1 percent. Returns are due April 30, moving to Monday if the date falls on a weekend. If you sell and move out of town, ask the treasurer's office how a part-year return works.

Transfer tax and recording

The seller owes two Michigan transfer taxes when the deed is recorded. The state rate is $3.75 for each $500 of price. The county adds 55 cents for each $500, a rate that applies to counties under 2,000,000 residents. At the Jackson County Register of Deeds you can combine the tax and the recording fee in one check made out to that office.

MCL 207.526 exempts gifts to a child or grandchild, title-correction deeds and security instruments, and the county register posts its own exemption guidance. Your title agent should show every line on the settlement statement so nothing surprises you at the table. Bring your deed and a photo ID to the title office, and ask whether the buyer or the seller covers the recording fee in your contract.

What helps a Jackson listing

Buyers who commute to Lansing, Ann Arbor or Detroit weigh the drive on I-94 and US 127, so state the exit and the drive time to each in your listing. Local landmarks give buyers a sense of the place:

  • Dawn Foods, family-owned, has been based in Jackson since 1920.
  • Reynolds Field, a general aviation airport of about 700 acres south of I-94, hosts the Jackson College Flight School and the annual Jackson Blues Festival in June.
  • The city's parks department runs 26 parks totaling 645 acres, and JATA buses run ten routes Monday through Saturday from a downtown station.

Almost the whole city lies inside Jackson Public Schools. Mention the district when buyers ask.

Steps for a cash sale or a listing

Any route to closing starts with the same homework. Dig out your newest summer and winter tax bills. Look through your records for any past rental registration. Settle who will pay for repairs. Then get a draft settlement statement from your title agent with the transfer tax shown. A cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal and the repair negotiations that often follow a buyer's inspection, and it lets you pick the closing date.

After closing, rescind your homestead exemption within 90 days if the house was your principal residence, and let Community Development know if tenants lived there.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What must a Jackson landlord tell the city after a sale?

Send Community Development the buyer's name and contact details within 45 days of the sale. The buyer then has 45 days from closing to register, unless they file for a 100 percent principal residence exemption.

When are Jackson summer property taxes due?

Either all at once by July 31 or in five installments on the 20th of each month from July to November. The winter bill can be paid from December 1 until February 14.

Does Jackson tax income?

Yes. Residents with more than $600 in income pay 1 percent and nonresident workers pay 0.5 percent, with returns due April 30.

What transfer tax does a Jackson seller pay?

The seller covers a state tax of $3.75 per $500 of price plus a county tax of 55 cents per $500. Both are due when the deed is recorded, and one check to the Register of Deeds can cover tax and fee together.

What is the deadline for a new Jackson owner's principal residence exemption?

The claim is due June 1 to cover the summer bill, and the buyer needs to own and live in the house by that date. A missed claim can still be fixed at the July Board of Review.

In Burton you can list with an agent, sell on your own, or strike a cash deal with a buyer who will take on the house's repairs. Whichever you choose, a deed gets recorded at the Genesee County Register of Deeds and transfer tax is paid on the price.

Choose by weighing how soon you must leave, the house's condition, and anything clouding the title, such as back taxes, a lien or an estate still in progress. Patience and a house that shows well favor a listing. A seller who needs a firm date is better served by cash.

  • Agent listing: more buyers, but showings, appraisal and a buyer's lender add delay.

Burton lies just outside Flint in Genesee County, and its roughly 29,300 residents make it the county's second largest city. Within city limits lie about 23 square miles of land. Older houses and water service

Look at the roof and heating system before showings, tell buyers what you know, and hold on to receipts for work you have paid for.

One recent change matters for utility costs: Burton began receiving Karegnondi Water Authority water, treated by the Genesee County Drain Commission, in December 2017. A buyer comparing monthly costs may ask about water bills, so keep a recent statement handy.

Permit rules to check before a sale

Burton's Building Division publishes plain rules that decide whether past work will cause trouble with a buyer. Getting a permit is the owner's job, and work done without one can surface during an inspection or the buyer's lender review.

  • A shed under 199 square feet needs a site permit; a structure of 200 square feet or more counts as a garage and needs a building permit.
  • Decks need permits unless they stand free at least 10 feet from the house and are under 200 square feet.
  • Finishing a basement requires a permit and an egress window.
  • In-ground pools need permits, and above-ground pools do when they stay up year round.
  • Cosmetic interior work such as paint and flooring needs no permit.

Walk the property with a notepad before anyone else does. Note the shed, any deck, a finished basement, a pool, and anything else that changed since you bought. Match each item against what the city has on file. A short list of mismatches is easy to explain to a buyer, while a surprise found by an inspector tends to cost you leverage.

If you built a deck or finished the basement yourself, call the Building Division through City Hall and ask what is on file. Fixing that gap before you list costs less than haggling over it later.

Property tax dates and the cap

The city bills twice a year, on its own calendar. Summer bills are mailed by July 1 and due September 30. A one-time 4% penalty hits on October 1, then half a percent accrues each month. Winter bills are mailed December 1 and due February 28. The city does not accept postmarks, so payment has to arrive at the Treasurer's office at 4303 S. Center Road by the due date.

On March 1 the account moves to the Genesee County Treasurer (810-257-3054), where a 4% collection fee and rising interest apply. Property left unpaid for two years is foreclosed and sold at auction.

Proposal A caps yearly growth in taxable value at the lesser of inflation or 5% for as long as the owner stays. A transfer can lift it to the state equalized value, so the buyer's first bill can be higher than yours. New principal residence exemption applications reach the assessor by June 1, and a change of residence calls for an update form.

Genesee County recording charges

A deed filed with the Genesee County Register of Deeds costs a flat $30, however long it is. For a warranty deed, a land contract or any deed with a covenant of warranty, the Genesee County Treasurer must certify taxes first, for $5 on a separate check.

The county posts $7.50 per thousand for the state and $1.10 per thousand for the county, which add up to $8.60. The seller is liable, and the base is the price paid. Mortgages carry no transfer tax in Michigan.

A few transfers escape the tax, such as a gift deed to your child or a deed given in lieu of foreclosure, and the deed itself has to cite the exemption.

Is a cash buyer right for your sale?

Cash can be the better path when the work a retail buyer would demand is worth more than the discount a cash buyer takes. That happens with houses needing a roof or mechanical work, estates with several heirs, and landlord-owned houses with unpaid rent.

Time also matters for the tax calendar. If you close between the summer and winter due dates, ask your closing agent to prorate what each side owes, and keep the receipt for any bill you paid at the Treasurer's office on South Center Road.

Gather your tax bill, any permit records and a recent water statement, and ask each buyer for a written offer that spells out who pays closing costs. Line up at least two before you sign anything.

Selling checklist

  1. Establish who may sign the deed, particularly when an estate is involved.
  2. Ask the Building Division, via City Hall, about open permits and occupancy sign-off.
  3. Settle the current tax bill and check whether anything slipped to the county after March 1.
  4. Have the treasurer's certification ordered when the deed carries a warranty.
  5. Name any exemption on the face of the deed.
  6. Mail the rescind form to the assessor after you move out.

Keep your latest water statement and tax bill within reach. They show a buyer what the house costs to run, and a buyer's agent or lender will ask for them early. Handing them over promptly makes you look prepared and leaves fewer openings to renegotiate.

A cash buyer can accept open permit questions and price accordingly. A mortgage buyer's lender may want them settled first, so choose early which buyer you are targeting.

Does Burton demand an inspection before closing?

Not as a general rule. The Building Division issues building, site and occupancy permits, so contact it through City Hall to learn if your address has open permits or needs an occupancy sign-off.

The combined rate is $8.60 for each $1,000 of price. By statute it is the seller's bill unless an exemption fits.

What are Burton's property tax deadlines?

Summer bills are due September 30 and winter bills February 28. Anything unpaid on March 1 moves to the Genesee County Treasurer, and fees and interest pile on.

Will unpermitted work block a Burton sale?

Not automatically, but buyers will ask about it. Because permits are the owner's responsibility, a buyer may want a lower price or want the work made legal. Cash buyers tend to take the house as is and price it in.

What becomes of my homestead exemption in a Burton sale?

It stops when the house is no longer your principal residence. File a Request to Rescind (Form 2602) with the city assessor inside 90 days, or pay $5 for each late day up to $200.

Choosing how to sell in Oak Park

An Oak Park owner can hire an agent, go it alone, or sell to someone who buys houses for cash. After any of them, three offices need paperwork: the city assessor, the Municipal Services Department, and the Oakland County deed office.

Much of Oak Park was built in the postwar boom, so a house often carries decades of updates, some permitted and some not. A buyer with a mortgage orders an inspection and an appraisal. A buyer without one prices repairs into the offer. Get closing date, repair terms and your net amount in writing from each, then compare the totals.

For 2020 to 2024 the middle owner-occupied value was $212,300, rent in the middle of the range was $1,396 a month, and owners lived in 63.3% of homes. The city counts 12,452 households with a middle income of $71,510.

The city assessor publishes a sales study each year. Reading both shows how the assessor treats houses like yours, which helps when weighing an offer.

Oak Park Schools serves most of the city. Homes between 10 Mile and 11 Mile Roads belong to the Berkley School District, and about a square mile at the east end is in Ferndale Public Schools. Two neighbors can be in different districts, so check the exact address.

City charges that can come up at a sale

ChargeAmount and when it applies

Permits a seller should be able to show

The city issues separate building, electrical and demolition permits, and the Building Division at 14300 Oak Park Boulevard takes building applications. Its Roofing Guidelines for Residential Properties describe the roofing permit and the inspections a roof job requires.

If a prior owner did the roof, wiring or an addition, ask Municipal Services what is on record for your address. A missing final sign-off is cheaper to resolve before listing than after a buyer's inspector spots it. City code also asks owners, occupants and tenants to maintain the ground around their buildings, so cut back overgrowth and haul out debris before showings. Clearing out a home is part of many sales. A residential garage sale needs a $10 permit from the City Clerk's Office, which asks for a state ID or driver's license showing the sale address.

Deed recording at the county

The deed goes to the Oakland County Register of Deeds. County transfer tax is 55 cents for each $500 of consideration and state tax is $3.75 for each $500. Consideration under $100.00 is exempt, and the reason for any exemption has to be written on the face of the document.

The office asks for notarized signatures, a 2-1/2 inch blank top margin, and an embossed seal on any death certificate filed. Its index reaches back to January 1, 1964, so you can pull your own earlier deed and confirm the legal description before signing. A warranty deed is first tax certified at the county treasurer's office for $5.00, and recording costs $30.00.

From signed offer to closing

Once you accept an offer, the work splits into a few short tasks. First, the closing agent orders title work and checks that no lien or unpaid tax sits on the parcel. Second, you confirm with Municipal Services whether the house needs a certificate of occupancy or a rental inspection, since a buyer cannot move in until those are settled. Third, the deed is prepared with notarized signatures and the correct margins so the county does not reject it.

After closing, the paperwork keeps moving. The deed is recorded at the county, the Property Transfer Affidavit goes to the assessor within 45 days, and you file the request to rescind your principal residence exemption. The buyer files a new exemption form. If you ran an alarm system, hand the permit information to the buyer.

What to bring when you call the city

Have your parcel number and street address ready before you phone Municipal Services or the Assessor's Office. Ask what is on record for permits, whether a certificate of occupancy applies, and whether a rental registration is still active for the house. Write down the name of the department and the date you called so your closing agent can follow up.

For a house that was rented, bring the lease dates and the last inspection record. For a house with a garage or shed you plan to remove, ask about the demolition permit before any work starts. These calls take a few minutes and usually save a delay at closing.

Frequently asked questions

Is an inspection required before an Oak Park house is sold?

The city requires a certificate of occupancy for new or altered buildings and a rental inspection every two years or after a change in tenancy. Ask Municipal Services whether your house, particularly one that has been rented, needs either before a buyer moves in.

What does a certificate of occupancy cost in Oak Park?

The fee schedule prints $50 for occupancy only and $50 for reissuance. Commercial and renovation certificates carry different amounts.

Should an Oak Park seller do anything about the alarm permit?

The city charges a one-time $20 fee and requires a new permit each time an operable alarm changes owners. Tell the buyer so they register the system in their own name.

What is the deadline for the Property Transfer Affidavit in Oak Park?

Forty-five days from the transfer, filed at the Assessor's Office, 14000 Oak Park Boulevard. It covers any change in title, beneficial use or ownership interest.

Where does the deed for an Oak Park house get filed?

At the Oakland County Register of Deeds. A warranty deed is first tax certified at the county treasurer's office for $5.00, and recording costs $30.00.

Selling in Southgate starts with a city certificate

Southgate won't let a residential sale move forward cleanly without a Certificate of Compliance, or a buyer's signed promise to fix whatever the city cites. Home Sales inspections began on July 12, 2021 and cover every dwelling in town, so put the certificate on your calendar before you pick a closing date.

Southgate is a Downriver suburb in Wayne County, about 14 miles southwest of downtown Detroit. It has 28,931 residents as of July 2025, down from 30,014 in 2020. The houses are mostly post-war and sit close together on short blocks, so buyers compare your listing against others a street or two away. Owner-occupied homes have a middle value of $173,600.

You can reach a buyer in three common ways:

  • An agent listing draws the most buyers and adds a lender, an appraisal and a wait.
  • A private sale leaves pricing, the contract and the inspection with you.
  • A cash purchase as-is lets the buyer take on the cited violations through a signed affidavit.

Whichever you pick, read the contract for who pays the inspection fee, who does repairs and when funds arrive.

How the Southgate resale inspection works

The city checks the outside of each dwelling before it changes hands. A certificate covers a single sale or transfer, and the next owner who sells needs a fresh inspection.

Southgate Home Sales inspection terms
StepWhat it involvesCost or timing
First inspectionExterior check of the dwelling$200 as of June 1, 2024
Extra visitsEach return trip after the first$60 per visit
ReportSent by email, mail or pickupWithin 5 business days of the visit
As-is escrowBuyer signs an affidavit and escrow agreement$1,000 deposited before closing

You have two paths. Path one is to correct each cited item and collect the certificate. Path two is to sell as-is: the buyer signs an affidavit assuming the violations, plus an escrow agreement, and deposits $1,000 before closing. That affidavit then doubles as the closing document.

Who to call and what to prepare

Home Sales is its own department at City Hall, separate from the Building Department, with its own line at (734) 258-7783. It answers on weekdays and closes for lunch between noon and 1:00 p.m.

The department's page links an application, an inspection checklist and an online invoice payment. Read the checklist before the inspector comes, so you can fix small items first and avoid paying for a second visit. Have the certificate or the buyer's signed affidavit in hand before you book a closing.

Steps for a Southgate sale

The city certificate and the county recording step both sit between an accepted offer and a closing, so line them up in order.

  2. Choose between correcting the cited items and letting the buyer assume them.
  3. Hold the certificate or the signed affidavit before a closing date is set.
  4. Have your title company line up tax certification for a warranty deed.
  5. Record the deed with the county and pay transfer tax then unless an exemption applies.

With the population down 3.6 percent since 2020, buyers may ask to see closed sales on nearby streets, so have a few ready.

Home values and ownership in Southgate

Owner-occupied homes have a middle value of $173,600, and 67.2 percent of homes have an owner living in them. Owners with a mortgage pay a middle monthly cost of $1,463, while owners with a paid-off house pay $580. Middle gross rent is $1,120 and middle household income is $66,118 (2020-2024 figures).

The 2020 count found 14,053 housing units, with 4.0 percent vacant and a rental vacancy rate of 5.4 percent. Shopping and restaurant strips help the city appeal to people moving within the area, and getting around is easy: I-75 clips the northwest corner and M-85 (Fort Street) runs along most of the eastern line. For a seller, the takeaway is a steady, compact market where condition and a clean certificate decide how fast an offer closes.

Recording a deed at the Wayne County Register of Deeds

Wayne County moved to a new fee schedule on January 1, 2026: a $26 base and a $4 state survey fee, which makes $30 per deed. Transfer tax comes due at recording unless a proper exemption is noted. The office prints $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state.

  • A warranty deed, a deed with a warranty covenant or a land contract needs Wayne County Treasurer certification before recording.
  • Cards need matching ID, and American Express and Discover are refused.
  • Mailed personal checks are accepted, counter ones are not, and each document needs its own check.
  • Phone: (313) 224-5851.

Have your title company confirm every figure at your price.

Selling a rented house in Southgate

Landlords should ask the Building Department which rental registration applies to the address, then ask Home Sales whether the sale still needs a certificate. The resale rule reaches all residential dwellings, rented or not.

A buyer who keeps the tenant will want the lease, the deposit amount and the payment record. Pull those together before you invite offers, and tell tenants early about inspection dates so the inspector can reach the exterior and any needed access. Keep the report you receive, because it shows the buyer exactly which items the city cited.

What happens at closing

By closing day the paperwork should already be settled. The certificate or the signed affidavit is in the file, the title company has lined up tax certification for the deed, and everyone knows who pays the inspection fee. If the buyer is assuming violations, the $1,000 escrow deposit is in place before the signing, and the affidavit serves as the closing document.

After the signing, the deed goes to the Wayne County Register of Deeds for recording, and transfer tax is paid at that point unless an exemption is noted. Ask your title company for the final figures at your actual price, and keep a copy of the certificate or affidavit with your sale records, since the next owner will need a fresh inspection anyway.

What a cash sale skips here

A cash buyer doesn't need a lender or an appraisal, so the wait for loan approval drops out of the schedule. The city's rules still apply, which is where the as-is path helps: the buyer takes on the cited violations by affidavit and escrow instead of you finishing repairs first. Put the escrow terms in the purchase agreement, confirm who pays the inspection fee, and set the funding date in writing before you sign.

Is a Certificate of Compliance required to sell in Southgate?

Yes, for residential dwellings sold since July 12, 2021. Either fix the cited items, or sell as-is with the buyer's signed affidavit and $1,000 escrow deposit before closing.

What does the Southgate resale inspection cost?

The first inspection is $200 as of June 1, 2024, and each later visit is $60. Confirm the amount with Home Sales before booking.

Does the Southgate certificate carry over to the next owner?

No. It covers one sale or transfer, and each later sale needs a new inspection.

What happens to Southgate deed fees at the county?

Wayne County charges $30 per document under its January 1, 2026 schedule, with transfer tax paid at recording. Your title company can total the figures.

Can a cash buyer close before Southgate repairs are finished?

Yes. The buyer signs the violation affidavit and escrows $1,000, and that affidavit becomes the closing document. Spell out the escrow terms in the purchase agreement.

What a Madison Heights homeowner should know before selling

Three local points shape a Madison Heights sale: the city sends its own property tax bills, it licenses landlords but skips resale inspections, and the transfer affidavit goes to an office on Thirteen Mile Road. Once those are handled, the closing follows the usual Michigan steps.

The 2025 estimate of 28,297 people sits 0.6% under the 2020 base. Owners occupy 64.8% of the homes, valued at a median of $199,100 for 2020 to 2024, while renters pay a median gross rent of $1,176. Median household income is $69,503.

The city and its neighborhoods

Madison Heights is a compact Oakland County city about 12 miles north of downtown Detroit. Troy, Royal Oak, Hazel Park and Warren ring the city, and its eastern edge at Dequindre Road doubles as the line between Oakland and Macomb counties. I-75 skirts the west side while I-696 marks much of the south. About 91% of its buildings are single-family homes or condominiums, roughly 9,800 owners, yet light industrial and commercial property supplies around 60% of the tax base.

Madison District Public Schools and Lamphere Public Schools serve different addresses, so confirm which one covers your street before you describe the school zone. Buyers also ask about commutes, and the highways on the west and south sides make that an easy point to include in the listing.

Will Madison Heights make me pass an inspection to sell?

No. City staff state that Madison Heights neither requires nor provides resale inspections, so you can list or sign a purchase agreement without booking a walk-through.

Rentals are a separate matter. An owner who lets someone else live in a Madison Heights house needs a landlord license, even when no rent is charged. A qualified relative living there waives both the fee and the inspection. Without a license, an owner cannot collect rent or evict, a point worth settling before a tenant-occupied house goes on the market.

Madison Heights landlord license fees
Property typeFee, new or renewal
Single-family home$210
Up to four units$245
Five or more units$47.50 per unit

The first license may run under three years with a prorated fee, and each renewal covers four years and brings a fresh inspection. The city will not issue a license while property taxes, special assessments or water bills are unpaid.

Tax bills and deadlines

The city's treasury handles both bills directly. Early July brings the summer bill, payable through August 31 with no penalty, and early December brings the winter bill, payable through February 17.

After August 31, a 4% penalty applies from September 1, and a further 1/2% accrues each month. Winter bills pick up a 3% penalty on February 18. City Hall stops taking payment after March 2, and from March 3 the Oakland County Treasurer collects, with extra penalties added. A drop box outside City Hall takes checks and money orders around the clock.

A sale reopens the next owner's number. In the year after a transfer, taxable value jumps to the state equalized value under MCL 211.27a, so a long-held house that has been capped for decades can produce a much larger bill for the buyer. If you took the principal residence exemption, file a rescission after you move out. MCL 211.7cc sets a 90-day window and charges $5 a day, to a maximum of $200, for lateness. Closing agents must give both sides the affidavit and rescission forms at the table.

Which documents and fees come with a Madison Heights closing?

A typical closing here involves a recorded deed, a tax certification if the deed carries a warranty, transfer tax and the city affidavit. A title company usually takes care of the deed work and the certificate.

  • Recording: Oakland County's Register of Deeds examines each document before recording it. The page needs a 2.5 inch margin at the top and a notary's signature.
  • Tax certification: taxes must show as current on a warranty deed, and the county charges $5.
  • Transfer tax: state and county tax together run $4.30 per $500 of price. Gifts to a child or grandchild are exempt under MCL 207.526.
  • City affidavit: file it with the Assessing Department at 300 W Thirteen Mile Road within 45 days. A late residential filing costs $5 a day up to $200, and commercial or industrial property costs $25 a day up to $1,000.

Ask the Oakland County Register of Deeds for the current recording fee before mailing anything. Its Sheriff Deed and Clerk Deed redemption desk is a separate service and does not affect an ordinary sale.

Which sale route fits a Madison Heights house?

Pick by how much time you have and what shape the house is in. Compare each route by the money left after repairs, carrying costs and closing fees, since a high list price can shrink quickly.

  • Agent listing: showings and wide exposure, with the buyer's lender and appraisal setting the timeline.
  • For sale by owner: full control of price and terms, and the disclosures and paperwork fall on you.
  • Cash purchase: no lender step, and the buyer takes the house with its repairs or a tenant already inside.

If a cash sale appeals, tell us the Madison Heights address and what shape the place is in, and we will price it as it stands.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Madison Heights houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

A short checklist before closing

Pull your latest tax bills and confirm both are paid or ready to be prorated, since City Hall stops taking payment after March 2 and the county takes over from there. If the house was rented, confirm the landlord license status, because the city will not issue one while taxes, special assessments or water bills are unpaid. Ask your title company to bring the affidavit and rescission forms to the table. After closing, send the transfer affidavit to the Assessing Department on time and file your own rescission within the 90-day window. A cash buyer can take over these steps with you, and because there is no lender, the buyer can usually close on the date you choose.

The paperwork has a rhythm. Before the sale, you deal with taxes and any landlord license. At the table, the title company handles the deed, the certificate and the transfer tax. Within 45 days, the buyer files the affidavit with the Assessing Department at 300 W Thirteen Mile Road. Within 90 days, you cancel the exemption on the house you left. If a tenant lives in the house, read the lease before you promise a possession date, and ask the buyer in writing whether the tenant will stay.

Frequently asked questions

Does Madison Heights inspect houses at resale?

No. The city does not require or provide resale inspections. Inspections come up only with landlord licensing, and an owner-occupied sale does not trigger one.

Can a tenant stay in the house while I sell it?

Yes, provided the house carries a city landlord license. The license is mandatory for any occupied home the owner does not live in, though a qualified relative waives the fee and inspection. Without it, rent collection and eviction are off the table.

What transfer tax does a Madison Heights seller owe?

State and county tax together come to $4.30 per $500 of price. The deed has to show the value or carry an affidavit stating it.

Where do I send Madison Heights taxes after March 2?

To the Oakland County Treasurer. City Hall accepts payment only through March 2, and the county adds penalties after that.

What happens if I file the transfer affidavit late?

The city fines $5 per day up to $200 for a residential property. The deadline is 45 days after the transfer, and the form goes to the Assessing Department.

Ways to sell in Port Huron

A Port Huron homeowner has three basic options: list with an agent, sell privately, or accept an offer from a buyer who purchases houses outright. The city is the St. Clair County seat, so the county land records office sits inside city limits.

How quickly a sale closes comes down to what is left unresolved. Clear title, permits on file and an empty house move fast on any route. An unpaid tax bill, a missing permit or a lease in place slows things, and the buyer either waits for a fix or discounts the price. The sections below cover what the city and county ask for, so you can clear those items early.

Port Huron home values

Port Huron stands where Lake Huron narrows into the St. Clair River, facing Sarnia, Ontario across the water, and the Blue Water Bridge links the two cities. The 2020 census counted 28,983 residents, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 28,273, a 2.4% decline.

The middle owner-occupied home was valued at $149,300 for 2020 to 2024, with a middle rent of $982. Owners live in 61.7% of the homes. The city has 12,734 households averaging 2.21 people, with a middle income of $50,366. Monthly owner costs sit around $1,140 with a mortgage and $562 without.

If you inherited the house, finish the title and probate steps before listing, and start them early. Recent nearby sales are the best guide to a fair price.

Water, flood maps and winter weather

With so much shoreline, flood mapping matters. The city's planning page links flood maps, and a property in a flood plain or zone may need EGLE Water Resources approval for exterior projects. Ask the Building Inspection Division whether your parcel is mapped before you list.

Winters bring 35.5 inches of snow in a typical year, spread over 22 snowy days, and the record low is minus 19 F. Buyers' inspectors look closely at roofs, gutters and heating, so have those in good shape. Water access is the main draw for buyers, since the city owns waterfront parks, public beaches and a large municipal marina system.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Port Huron house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Permits that come up before a sale

Port Huron's Building Inspection Division sorts permits into four groups, and a buyer's inspector tends to look at the same items.

Port Huron permit categories
Permit typeWork covered
Building permitRoofs, windows, doors, siding, decks, porches, garages, basement finishes, interior and exterior alterations
Zoning permitFences, driveways, concrete patios, hot tubs, playground equipment, pools over 24 inches deep
Mechanical permitFurnaces, air conditioners, hot water tanks, fireplaces, gas piping
Electrical permitNew circuits, water heaters, sump pumps, generators, smoke detectors
No permit neededPainting, carpeting, tile, replacing kitchen cabinets in the same layout

Going without a permit can lead to safety problems, fines, even removal of the structure, and complications when you try to sell. An owner may pull permits in place of a contractor only as the registered legal owner living in the house as a primary residence. Properties in the Historic District need Historic District Commission approval for exterior work. The Building Inspection Division answers at (810) 984-9733.

Rental and vacant houses

The planning department runs a Rental Certification Program, and its document center posts a Foreclosed, Vacant and Abandoned Property Registration Form. If your house has been rented or sits empty, ask the Building Inspection Division what registration or certification applies to the address and whether it passes to a buyer.

Houses inside the historic area fall under Chapter 52-576 through 52-591 of the city's Historic District ordinance, which requires a work permit for alterations, significant repairs, new construction, demolition and moving.

St. Clair County land records office

You will find the register's office at 200 Grand River Avenue, Suite 103, Port Huron, reachable at (810) 989-6930. Monday through Thursday it works from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday from 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a lunch closing from noon to 1:00 p.m. The recording counter shuts at 4:00 p.m., and anything received later is dated 8:00 a.m. on the next business day.

  • Recording charge: a flat $30.00 for each document whatever its page count, plus $3.00 after the first instrument reference.
  • Certified copy of a recorded document: $5.00.
  • Tax certificate: required before recording a warranty deed, a land contract, or any deed with a warranty covenant, under MCL 211.135. The treasurer certifies over the counter from 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., closed noon to 1:00 p.m.
  • Transfer tax: $1.10 for each thousand dollars of sale amount for the county and $7.50 for each thousand for the state.

Online records go back to 1984, and there is a Property Fraud Alert sign-up. Closing agents normally carry the deed in for the seller.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Port Huron houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Getting the paperwork ready

Before you list, pull your deed, any probate papers, permit records and the latest tax bill. Call the Building Inspection Division about flood zones, rental certification and vacant property registration, then ask your closing agent to schedule the recording early enough to beat the 4:00 p.m. counter cutoff on closing day. If an unpaid tax bill or lease is involved, settle how it will be handled in the contract so the buyer is not surprised.

Clearing problems before buyers see the house

Most delays in a Port Huron sale trace back to three things: title, taxes and occupancy. Order a title check early so any lien or probate gap shows up while you still have time to fix it. Ask the county treasurer for the current tax status, and pay what is owed or plan to settle it from the proceeds at closing. If a tenant lives in the house, decide whether they will stay through closing or leave first, and keep the lease handy for every buyer who asks.

An empty house is easier to show and to close on. Turn on the heat in cold months, keep the yard tidy, and keep the receipts for any roof, furnace or window work so the buyer's inspector sees a documented history.

Listing, private sale or direct buyer on the calendar

A listing adds showings, a buyer's loan approval, an appraisal and a repair negotiation, and each of those can add days. A private sale removes the agent but leaves you to handle the contract and the paperwork. A direct purchase can close once title is clear and the recording is scheduled. Ask each buyer for a closing date, a net figure and a list of who pays for recording, the tax certificate and transfer tax, then compare the offers on those terms rather than the headline price alone.

How soon can a Port Huron sale close?

It depends on title, taxes and any tenant. At the recording end, the St. Clair County counter closes at 4:00 p.m., and a document received after that is dated 8:00 a.m. the next business day.

Do I need a permit for work I did before selling in Port Huron?

Roofs, windows, doors, siding, decks, garages and basement finishes need a building permit, and furnaces, water heaters and sump pumps need trade permits. Skipping one can cause problems when you sell.

Where is a Port Huron deed recorded?

At the St. Clair County Register of Deeds, 200 Grand River Avenue, Suite 103. A warranty deed needs a county treasurer's tax certificate first.

What transfer tax applies in St. Clair County?

The county charges $1.10 per thousand dollars of sale amount and the state charges $7.50 per thousand. Your closing statement shows the exact dollar amounts for your sale.

Are there flood zones to check before listing in Port Huron?

Yes. The city links flood maps on its planning page, and a property in a flood plain may need state approval for exterior projects. Call the Building Inspection Division at (810) 984-9733 to learn whether your parcel is mapped.

The city inspection comes first

No Allen Park house closes without a Certificate of Occupancy or a signed buyer affidavit, and either one takes some days to arrange. The rule covers homes first listed on or after March 1, 2022, under Chapter 10, Article 10, Section 10-404 of the city code. A house listed before that date is outside it.

Build your schedule backward from the closing date. Request the inspection first, read what the inspector cites, and then choose between repairing the items yourself and handing them to a buyer who accepts them.

How the sales inspection works

The Building Department walks the interior and the outside of the lot. The fee of $175 pays for both the first visit and the follow-up. The city posts a list of the most common violations and an application form, so you can check your own house before the inspector arrives.

  • Fix every cited item and the department issues the Certificate of Occupancy.
  • Or sell as is, which requires the buyer to sign an affidavit accepting the violations.
  • The buyer also puts at least $500 into escrow, and 10 percent of it cannot be refunded.
  • That affidavit takes the place of the certificate as the closing document.
  • Reports can be mailed or picked up within 5 business days of the inspection.

On inspection day, make sure the inspector can reach every room and the outside of the lot. Unlock sheds and garages, clear access to the furnace and electrical panel, and leave any past repair receipts where you can find them. If a tenant lives there, coordinate the visit with them first.

Phone the Building Department at 313-928-4441 or 313-928-4134 to schedule. The city's advice to sellers is plain: do not set a closing date until you hold the certificate or the buyer's signed affidavit.

Allen Park in brief

Allen Park is a Downriver city of 7.00 square miles, about 12 miles from downtown Detroit. The 2020 count was 28,638 residents, and the mid-2025 estimate is 27,445. Population peaked at 40,747 in 1970, which is why so many of its brick houses date from the postwar boom. Owners occupy 87.3% of homes, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $183,700, and typical rent is $1,246 a month. Owners with a mortgage pay about $1,473 a month, and median household income is $81,655. Only 3.8 percent of the 12,252 housing units stood vacant in 2020, so the market is stable.

School district depends on the street. Most of the city sits in the Allen Park School District, the north end is part of Melvindale-Northern Allen Park Public Schools, and the area south of the Sexton-Kilfoil Drain falls in the Southgate Community School District. Put the district name in your listing, since families shopping by school will filter by it.

Recording a deed in Wayne County

Recording costs $30 per document, split as $26 for the register plus a $4 state survey and remonumentation fee. That schedule started January 1, 2026, the first increase at the office since 1996.

Transfer tax comes due at recording, at $3.75 per $500 for the state and $0.55 per $500 for the county. Together that is $8.60 for each thousand dollars of price, and the seller bears it. Warranty deeds must carry a certification from the Wayne County Treasurer before they are recorded.

Payment rules here differ from other counties:

  • Debit and credit cards work over the counter with matching ID, and are refused for mailed items.
  • A personal check can be mailed, but the counter will not take one.
  • The office does not process American Express or Discover.
  • One check per document, for the exact total: an overpayment above $25 returns the papers.

The office answers questions at (313) 224-5851.

Why the register rejects deeds

The office publishes its own list of repeat offenders. Photocopied signatures fail. So does a deed with no stated price and no exemption cited, a thin legal description, a notary block that is hard to read, or no return address for the recorded copy. Parcel number and street address belong on the page as well.

One flawed document sinks a whole bundle paid with a single check. Have the drafter run the checklist ahead of closing and confirm the treasurer has certified the deed.

If the Allen Park house is a rental

Every rental house must hold a Certificate of Compliance before anyone occupies it. Registration costs $200 at first, renewal costs $175, and each certificate lasts three years.

City rental inspectors work Tuesdays and Thursdays only, using the same Building Department phone numbers as the sales inspection. Landlords whose house is not rented can file a non-rental affidavit. If a tenant lives in the house when you sell, expect scheduling work for the interior inspection, and a buyer who will keep renting should ask for the date of your current certificate. Keep the certificate, the registration receipt and any inspection notes together in one folder. Handing the buyer that folder at the start shows the house has been run properly and shortens the questions that follow, which helps when you want a fast closing.

A cash sale and the inspection

A cash buyer fits this process well when the house has cited items you do not want to fix. The buyer signs the affidavit, escrows the deposit, and takes on the repairs after closing, so you skip contractors and re-inspection. You still owe the $175 inspection fee and the recording and tax steps above, and the city still wants the inspection requested before a closing date is set.

Think about what a cash sale skips. There is no lender appraisal, so a low appraisal cannot sink the deal. There are no repair requests after a buyer's inspection, and no wait while a buyer's loan is approved. The closing day is often negotiable. What it does not skip is the city paperwork, the tax certification on a warranty deed, or the recording step, so confirm each one with the buyer before you agree to terms.

Whoever you sell to, work in this order: schedule the inspection, read the report, choose repairs or the affidavit, confirm the treasurer's certification for a warranty deed, and only then fix a closing date.

Frequently asked questions

Which Allen Park homes are exempt from the occupancy certificate?

Homes that were listed before March 1, 2022. Anything listed on or after that date needs the certificate or a buyer's signed affidavit before closing.

What do I get for the $175 city inspection fee?

One initial walk-through and one final visit. Reports are mailed or held for pickup within 5 business days.

How do I estimate transfer tax on an Allen Park house?

Take the price in thousands and multiply by $8.60. That blends the state share of $3.75 per $500 with the county share of $0.55 per $500, and the seller pays it.

Where does an Allen Park deed get recorded?

At the Wayne County Register of Deeds, which has charged $30 per document since January 1, 2026. Warranty deeds go to the county treasurer for certification first.

Can I close with open violations on the house?

Yes, if the buyer signs the city affidavit and escrows at least $500. The buyer then handles the repairs after closing.

What a Hamtramck seller deals with first

Hamtramck is a two-square-mile city in Wayne County that sits almost entirely inside Detroit's borders, so a sale here follows Hamtramck's own city code and Wayne County's tax process, which differ from Detroit's. Whether the house goes to market, to a neighbor, or to a cash buyer, it passes three local checkpoints: the city's pre-sale inspection rules, the treasurer's tax calendar, and the assessor's transfer paperwork.

The city covers 2.09 square miles, all of it land, and Interstate 75 runs roughly along its western edge with I-94 near the southern edge. Downtown Detroit is about 5 miles south. Mid-2025 estimates count 27,261 people, 4.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base. Expect sales to be decided block by block rather than by a citywide trend.

Housing stock and household size

Most of the older homes trace back to the factory boom of the 1910s and 1920s. That history explains what a buyer finds inside a typical house: compact lots, frame houses and flats built close together, and many decades of owners making their own repairs. Houses that changed hands inside one family for generations often carry unrecorded repairs, old liens or unclear titles, so clear those up before you pick an asking price.

Survey estimates for 2020 through 2024 give a starting point for pricing:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $131,000.
  • Homeownership: 58.3 percent among 7,120 households.
  • Persons per household: 3.86, which points to large households and heavily used kitchens and baths.
  • Typical rent: $989 a month.

Because of those household sizes, a house with extra bedrooms or a finished basement often draws more interest than the same square footage elsewhere. Say plainly in your listing or conversation which rooms are legal bedrooms.

Do I need a city inspection to sell?

Only for some owners. Under the city's pre-sale subchapter (sections 150.201 to 150.206), a property holding a Neighborhood Enterprise Zone certificate cannot change hands, through a broker or otherwise, unless the Building Department has issued a current certificate of approval. Everyone else may request a voluntary inspection, but once you file that request you cannot withdraw it, and every violation found must be fixed to earn the certificate.

The same code gives you a way through if repairs would delay closing. The city refuses a transfer affidavit for an NEZ home that lacks the certificate, with one exception: the buyer may sign a notarized statement promising to fix every listed violation within six months. A few more details matter:

  • Both the inspection report and the certificate of approval last twelve months.
  • If the building official sees serious neglect or hazards, a mandatory inspection can be ordered whatever the NEZ status.
  • A certificate guarantees nothing about condition, and the city accepts no liability for concealed defects, mold or asbestos.

Before signing a purchase agreement, call the Building Department and ask whether your parcel has an NEZ certificate.

Vacant, foreclosed and rental houses

Chapter 96 of the city code covers houses that have sat empty. A home vacant for 180 days or more, or one that any lender, county or other holder has foreclosed, cannot be occupied until the Department of Public Services issues a certificate of occupancy. Getting it takes an inspection, correction of every violation, and payment of back property tax, special assessments, water and sewer bills and city cleanup charges.

Rentals fall under Chapter 150. Landlords hold a certificate of compliance good for two years at first and three years at each renewal. A sale ends that certificate at once, and the buyer has 30 days after the ownership change to apply for a new one. A landlord with a notice of violation outstanding must hand the buyer a copy and file the buyer's notarized acknowledgment with the building official before conveying the property, land contracts included.

Tax deadlines and what follows

Bills come out on July 1 and December 1 and are paid at the city treasurer's office. Whatever remains after the city's February 28 cutoff passes to the Wayne County Treasurer, where the cost climbs. The table follows a parcel that stays unpaid.

March 31 and April 1, a year after forfeitureCourt judgment; ownership moves to the county unless the owner redeems

Foreclosed homes are then offered at public auction in September and October, so a seller with two years of arrears has a hard deadline.

Assessor paperwork after a sale

Buyers have 45 days after closing to file a Property Transfer Affidavit with the assessor, and late filers can be charged $5 a day, capped at $200. Sellers sign a rescission request for their principal residence exemption so the claim leaves the parcel, since a missed rescission can turn into a bill if the state audits. A buyer who moves in files a fresh exemption affidavit, worth 18 mills of school operating tax.

State law also uncaps taxable value on a sale (MCL 211.27a). For the next calendar year it equals the state equalized value, roughly half of market price, which can push the buyer's first bill above yours. Assessment appeals go to the March Board of Review.

Transfer tax on a Hamtramck deed

Michigan puts the transfer tax on the seller: $3.75 per $500 of price at the state level (MCL 207.525) plus a county levy under MCL 207.504 of 55 cents per $500 below 2,000,000 residents, capped at 75 cents above that. The county treasurer collects both within 15 days after the deed is handed over.

MCL 207.526 exempts family conveyances to a child or grandchild, judgments that name no price, and deeds issued in foreclosing government-backed loans. Confirm the county rate and the recording fee with Wayne County before closing.

Local income tax

Hamtramck is one of the Michigan cities with its own income tax, at 1.00 percent for residents and 0.50 percent for nonresidents. Ask the city income tax office how a move out of town or rental income affects your filing.

Putting the steps in order

Call the Building Department first and ask whether your parcel holds an NEZ certificate, because that answer decides whether an inspection is mandatory. Then ask the treasurer which bills are open and whether anything has gone to Wayne County. If the house has been empty for months or came out of foreclosure, ask the Department of Public Services what it needs before it will issue a certificate of occupancy.

With those answers, sort the sale routes. A buyer who pays cash and accepts the house as it stands can simply sign the notarized promise to fix the violations, which keeps a sale moving when you cannot afford repairs before closing. Whichever buyer you choose, put in writing who files which forms and who pays for each repair, and give the closing agent the tax payoff early.

Frequently asked questions

Is a certificate of approval mandatory for my Hamtramck sale?

Only when the property holds a Neighborhood Enterprise Zone certificate. Other owners may ask for a voluntary inspection, though a filed request cannot be pulled back. In an NEZ sale, a buyer can offer a notarized repair promise in place of the certificate.

When is the Hamtramck summer tax bill due?

August 20 for the full amount. Paying half in July moves the rest to December 30. Winter bills are due February 15, and unpaid balances pass to Wayne County on March 1.

What is the foreclosure timeline for unpaid Hamtramck taxes?

About two years from the first delinquency. Wayne County takes over on March 1, forfeits the parcel a year later, and a circuit court judgment follows. Owners can redeem through March 31 of the foreclosure year by paying taxes, interest and fees.

Which forms follow a Hamtramck closing?

The buyer files a transfer affidavit within 45 days, and the seller files a rescission of the principal residence exemption. A buyer who will live there also files a new exemption affidavit.

Does a Hamtramck rental certificate carry over to a buyer?

No. The certificate ends at the sale, and the new owner applies for another within 30 days of the ownership change.

Why the inspection sets the pace in Garden City

A house cannot change occupants in Garden City until the city issues a certificate of occupancy, so the inspection calendar often matters more than the buyer's financing. The city is a compact Wayne County suburb of 5.87 square miles, roughly 15 miles west of downtown Detroit. Book the inspection early and plan the closing date around it. Sellers who wait often find the calendar full.

Small lots and older houses

Population climbed from 9,012 in 1950 to 38,017 in 1960 and topped out at 41,864 in 1970, before easing to 27,380 in 2020. Because the city grew so fast, much of the housing is more than 60 years old.

  • Lots as small as 40 by 135 feet leave little room for additions or large outbuildings.
  • Ford Road and Middlebelt Road are the main corridors for commuting and errands.
  • Older systems such as roofs, furnaces and wiring are the items an inspector is most likely to list.

Garden City housing figures

This is a city of homeowners, with nearly four of every five homes occupied by their owners.

Estimated residents, mid-202526,280

Headcount slipped 4.1% from the April 2020 base, so a seller should not wait for a wave of newcomers. A price that reflects the house's true condition moves a sale along faster.

Certificate of occupancy

When a property is sold, the city requires a certificate of occupancy in place before the buyer moves in. The Building Department schedules the inspection, which takes place Monday through Thursday, with a morning window from 9 a.m. to noon and an afternoon window from noon to 4 p.m. The fee is $200, payable when the inspection date is booked, and the certificate is good for one year.

Spring and summer are busy, and a seller may wait three to six weeks for an inspection. Someone who needs a fast closing should reserve the slot the day a contract is signed, or sooner. The Building Department number is (734) 793-1650.

  • Reserve an inspection date when the home is listed or under contract.
  • Fix visible safety items first, since a failed inspection means a reinspection and more waiting.
  • A December or January certificate is ready for an immediate closing.

Repairs that need a permit

Each permit lasts six months, and every required inspection has to be done within that time. A building permit covers roofs, windows, exterior doors, siding, gutters and kitchen or bathroom remodels. Mechanical permits cover water tanks, furnaces, air conditioners and generators. Service panels, circuits, fixtures and hard-wired smoke detectors need electrical permits, and sewer repairs, sinks, toilets and showers need plumbing permits. Driveways, easement walks, patios and porch caps fall under a flatwork permit.

A shed under 200 square feet skips the building permit, though its slab still needs flatwork approval. An owner living in the house may pull personal permits, and anyone who hires a contractor should require the contractor to pull them, at the same cost. Ask the Building Department whether any open permit on the address could affect the certificate before you list.

If the house is a rental

Garden City runs a rental certification program through its Ordinance Department at the police department, reachable at (734) 793-1748. Rental certifications run three years, and the owner must recertify before the term ends. A landlord selling the house should confirm that the certification is current and say whether tenants will stay.

An investor buying it should ask the Ordinance Department how the transfer affects that certification.

Services a buyer will ask about

Residents receive a free 95-gallon trash container from the city's refuse contractor, and curbside recycling carts can be delivered on request. Yard waste pickup runs from the first full week of April until about the middle of December, with Christmas trees collected after December 25. Buyers ask about these basics, so work them into your listing description.

Transfer tax and filings after closing

The seller carries both Michigan transfer taxes: the county charges 55 cents and the state $3.75 for each $500 of price (MCL 207.504 and 207.525). Payment reaches the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivering the deed (MCL 207.523). Your settlement statement has the exact total.

The buyer then notifies the assessor within 45 days so taxable value can reset to the state equalized value the next year (MCL 211.27a). Ask the assessor for an estimate of the new owner's bill, and keep the closing agent's settlement statement for your own tax records.

When an as-is sale makes sense

A tidy house on a standard lot may do fine on the open market, but the inspection queue and loan approval both stretch the timeline. A house that needs work to pass the certificate of occupancy, an estate property, or a seller facing a short deadline often does better with an as-is purchase.

  • A listing fits a house in good repair when you can wait out the inspection queue.
  • An as-is buyer fits a house where the inspector will likely list repairs you would rather not manage.
  • Get written agreement on who pays the inspection fee and handles any reinspection.

Weigh offers by what you keep after transfer tax, prorated taxes and credits, and write the closing date into the contract.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Working through a sale step by step

Call the Building Department the day you decide to sell and ask for the next open inspection date. While you wait, walk the house yourself. Look at smoke detectors, handrails, outlets, the furnace and the water heater, because simple safety items are the usual reasons a house fails the first visit. Do the cheap fixes yourself, and keep every receipt in one folder for the inspector and the buyer.

Once you have a contract, tell the buyer when the inspection is booked and agree in writing on who pays if a reinspection is needed. Ask the assessor for an estimate of the new owner's bill so the buyer is not surprised. Then ask the closing agent to confirm that the certificate, the transfer tax and any tax proration are ready before the signing date. A buyer who plans to occupy the house right away needs the certificate in hand, and a late inspection is the most common reason a Garden City closing slips. Build a few spare days into your move-out plan for that reason.

Frequently asked questions

Must a Garden City house pass inspection before it changes hands?

Yes. The city requires a certificate of occupancy whenever a property is sold, and the new owner cannot occupy the house without it. The Building Department at (734) 793-1650 books the inspection.

How long is the wait for the Garden City inspection?

A seller may wait three to six weeks in spring and summer. Booking early, or aiming for winter, shortens the wait.

What does the Garden City certificate of occupancy cost?

The fee is $200, paid when the inspection is scheduled, for a certificate good for one year. Confirm the amount with the Building Department.

Will a Garden City buyer's tax bill run higher than mine?

Often. Taxable value resets to the state equalized value in the calendar year after the transfer, and the buyer must notify the assessor within 45 days.

Can I still sell a house that fails the inspection?

Yes, but the certificate has to be issued before the new owner moves in. Some sellers make the repairs, and others sell as-is and let the buyer finish them and request the reinspection.

Rental and vacant home rules

Two city programs can touch your sale: one for rentals and one for empty houses. Community Development registers each detached one-family home that is leased or advertised for lease, and it runs its own list of vacant homes.

  • Rental registration costs $200, the permit to occupy $50, and the yearly renewal $250, due December 31.
  • Instead of filing a self-certification checklist, an owner can pay $155 for a city interior inspection.
  • A $100 penalty applies to a first failure to register, and civil infraction tickets can follow.
  • Whoever buys an existing rental has 30 days after the sale to re-register and get a fresh permit.
  • An empty house must be registered within 30 days, at a $355 fee shown on the vacant-home form.

A letter from the city about registering is not proof that you are renting, because the city targets homes not claimed as a homestead. Return a Statement of Exemption for a non-rental home and no fee applies. Even a house where a relative lives rent-free can count as a rental. Community Development is at 1827 N. Squirrel Road, phone 248-364-6900.

If you are the seller of a rental, gather the registration, the permit to occupy and any inspection results before you list. An investor taking over the tenants will ask for them first. If the house is empty, check whether it was ever put on the vacant registry, since a missing registration is easier to fix before a buyer's attorney finds it. An heir who has never lived in the house should check the vacant home registry requirement right away.

Auburn Hills housing at a glance

Just over half of homes, 51.3 percent, are owner-occupied, and the rest are rented. The average household has 2.10 people. The city grew 6.4 percent between 2020 and 2025 to an estimated 25,925 people, and the median age is 31.7.

The 2020 census counted 11,032 housing units with 7.1 percent vacant, and 37.0 percent of the 10,253 households were one person living alone. Buyers here include single professionals and small households, so a compact, low-maintenance house reads well.

Jobs, schools and parks buyers ask about

Car-industry work shapes local demand. More than 50 automotive corporations have facilities in town, with Stellantis headquartering its North American operations here. Great Lakes Crossing Outlets and the office parks draw people in daily, and the drive from most houses to those jobs is short, which a seller can mention in a listing.

Addresses fall into one of three school districts: Avondale, Pontiac or Rochester Community Schools. Every Avondale resident is zoned to Avondale High School in Auburn Hills. A Pontiac school, Will Rogers Elementary, sits in the northeast corner. Say which district applies in your listing, because families search by it.

Outdoor space counts too. Civic Center Park offers nature trails, a fishing pond, a softball field, tennis courts and a nine-hole disc golf course, the skate park is free from April to November, and a 2.1 mile crushed stone stretch of the 16-mile Clinton River Trail crosses the city. Oakland University and Oakland Community College each run a campus in the city.

Recording a deed in Oakland County

The Oakland County Register of Deeds records the deed. Any warranty deed, land contract or deed with a warranty clause needs a stamp from the Oakland County Treasurer first. The office takes calls at 248-858-0597 on weekdays.

Transfer tax is split between state and county: $3.75 per $500 to the state and 55 cents per $500 to the county, which together make $8.60 per $1,000 of price. It falls on the seller. Oakland is a charter county, so ask the office for its current recording fee.

Bring or send the signed, notarized deed with the grantee's address, the legal description and the price or exemption statement. A deed missing any of those can be returned, and a returned deed delays the closing. Your title company or closing attorney normally handles the submission, so ask them which vendor they use and when to expect confirmation.

Electronic recording works through approved vendors. The county's MiPropDocs tool excludes deeds, which transfer ownership, so a deed goes through a vendor or the office counter.

What the assessor needs after a sale

After closing, the buyer has 45 days to file a Property Transfer Affidavit. Residential filings that arrive late are charged $5 a day, up to $200. The assessor's office is open weekdays, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Property status is fixed as of tax day, which is December 31 of the prior year. Assessed value is half of true cash value, and taxable value is the lesser of state equalized value and the capped value. The cap grows with inflation or 5 percent, whichever is lower, until ownership changes.

  • Sellers rescind their exemption on the old home with Form 2602, within 90 days of moving out.
  • Buyers who move in before the May 1 deadline claim theirs with Form 2368.
  • A buyer moving in between June 2 and November 1 can claim it for winter taxes that year.

Closing agents are expected to bring both forms, though the law gives no remedy if one forgets. Ask yours at the start whether the forms are in the closing packet.

Selling an Auburn Hills house step by step

  1. Decide if the house counts as a rental or a vacant home, then register it or return the exemption statement.
  2. Call Community Development at 248-364-6900 to ask whether any city step applies to your address before you pick a closing date.
  3. Have the closing agent request the treasurer's stamp on any warranty deed.
  4. Set aside the transfer tax, which you owe at recording.
  5. File Form 2602 within 90 days of moving out, and remind the buyer about the 45 day affidavit.

Keep copies of everything you file or receive, including registration receipts, the exemption statement and the recording confirmation. If a question comes up months later, paper in your own files settles it quicker than a phone call to a city office.

A cash buyer can shorten the calendar by skipping the appraisal and the lender's timeline. The city's registration and the county's recording steps still apply, so confirm both up front. If the house is an existing rental, tell the buyer about the 30 day window to register again, because a missed deadline brings the $100 penalty.
