Frequently asked questions

Is a pre-sale inspection required in Auburn Hills?

The city's rules for sellers center on rental and vacant home registration. Ask Community Development at 248-364-6900 whether any step applies to your house before you pick a closing date.

How is transfer tax figured on an Auburn Hills sale?

It is $8.60 per $1,000 of price, and the seller pays it. The state takes $3.75 per $500 and the county takes 55 cents per $500.

What happens to rental registration when a rental sells?

The buyer registers again and gets a new permit to occupy within 30 days, paying $200 for registration and $50 for the permit.

Which county records deeds for Auburn Hills?

Oakland County. The Register of Deeds records the deed, and warranty deeds need a county treasurer certification first.

How long does a buyer have to report the sale to the city assessor?

Forty-five days. A late residential filing costs $5 per day, capped at $200.

How Walker homeowners sell quickly

A Walker owner can work with an agent, search for a buyer alone, or sell to a cash buyer who accepts the property as is. The city sits in Kent County beside Grand Rapids, so its market moves with the larger metro area.

Timing and condition pick the route. A tidy house with weeks to spare usually fares best on the open market. Deferred repairs, a tenant or an estate can make a buyer without a lender appraisal the easier match.

  • Agent: more exposure and a likelier top price, against a commission and a longer path to closing.
  • Alone: no commission, though contract, disclosures and deed fall to you.
  • Cash: fewer conditions and a set closing date, typically at a lower price than a polished listing.

Put every offer in writing, including who pays transfer tax and title costs, and note the date you expect to receive your funds.

The Walker market

Walker incorporated as a city in 1962, which kept Grand Rapids from annexing it. It has 25,881 residents as of 2025, up 2.9% from the 2020 base, and covers 24.58 square miles. I-96 forms the northern side, US 131 touches the northeast, Alpine Avenue (M-37) joins the interstate, and Lake Michigan Drive (M-45) cuts across the center. Meijer and Bissell are both headquartered here.

Homes carry a median value of $295,200. Owners live in 65.2% of homes, so many Walker units are rentals. The 20.2-minute average commute is short, and buyers working along I-96 or downtown value that access.

School districts serving Walker

Four public school districts serve the city: Comstock Park Public Schools, Grand Rapids Public Schools, Grandville Public Schools and Kenowa Hills Public Schools. Kenowa Hills runs Central Elementary and Zinser Elementary inside the city and zones its middle and high school students to buildings in Alpine Township. Cummings Elementary, from Grandville, and Walker Charter Academy are also in the city limits.

Covenant Christian High School and Hope Protestant Reformed Christian School are private options in Walker, and the Kent District Library has a Walker branch.

Four districts share one small city, so the district for a house can change from one block to the next. Name the district in the listing and ask Walker's assessor to confirm it for your parcel.

Walker tax bills and the city income tax

Walker's summer bill goes out July 1 and is due September 14, and the winter bill goes out December 1 and is due February 14. Summer carries over 90% of the year's tax. Payment must arrive by 5 p.m. on the due date, and a postmark does not count.

  • Late summer payments: 1% interest begins September 15, 4% more October 1, then 1% each month from November to February.
  • Late winter payments: a 3% penalty begins February 15.
  • Real property taxes still open on March 1 pass to the Kent County Treasurer.

Each bill includes a 1% administration fee. A principal residence earns relief from 18 school operating mills when the owner lives there on May 1 and has filed the exemption affidavit with Walker's assessor. After a sale, Michigan law resets the buyer's taxable value in the calendar year following the transfer.

The city also taxes income, 1% for residents and one-half of 1% for non-residents, through its Income Tax Department at 616-791-6880. Ask the income tax office whether any gain from your sale is reportable on the city return. The treasurer is open Monday through Thursday until 5 p.m. and Friday until 11:30 a.m.

Building and code rules

No rental certification program exists in Walker. Each property must instead meet the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code as amended in City Code Section 18-90, and staff act on complaints rather than patrolling.

The city lists the usual complaints, with their code sections, so a seller can check a house before listing:

  • Accumulations of junk and inoperable vehicles, under Section 50-142.
  • Tall grass and noxious weeds, under Section 90-3.
  • Fences, accessory structures, and parking on the lawn, under Chapter 94.
  • Recreational vehicle and trailer storage.
  • Sidewalk snow removal, under Section 70-68.

Code Enforcement can be reached at (616) 735-6129. Building inspections and plan review are contracted to Professional Code Inspections, and permits can be applied for through the BS&A portal or on paper. A certificate of occupancy is issued after the final inspections and zoning items are approved. The Community Development office at 4243 Remembrance Rd. NW takes calls at 616-791-6858.

Researching records and permits

The city runs its records through the BS&A Online portal. A visitor can search assessing records, view property sale data, look up current taxes, find permit and inspection history, and see the registered rental properties in the municipality. Searches work by address, owner name or parcel number.

The same portal handles building permit applications and inspection scheduling. The city publishes separate guides for new construction, remodels, pools and spas, accessory buildings and decks, and a Kent County Health Department environmental review form is part of the packet where it applies. A buyer who sees an unpermitted deck or finished basement in the inspection can use these guides to learn what the city would require.

Most questions about permits and zoning go to staff at the Community Development office.

Before you list, search your own parcel in the portal. You can see your tax status, your permit history and any inspection records, and you can hand a buyer the same information. Gathering it early means fewer surprises when a buyer's inspector asks about a deck, a finished basement or an older permit.

Recording a Walker deed in Kent County

Deeds for Walker properties go to the Kent County Register of Deeds in the County Administration Building at 300 Monroe Avenue NW in Grand Rapids. The office does not supply blank deeds or give advice on preparing them, so a title company or a Michigan real property attorney usually drafts the document.

Transfer tax is based on the consideration paid. The state rate is $3.75 for each $500 of value (MCL 207.525), the seller is liable (MCL 207.523), and the county rate is set by MCL 207.504 at 55 cents per $500 in a county of under 2,000,000 people. Ask the Register of Deeds for the current county amount and the recording fee, because fee schedules change.

Exempt transfers need a citation to MCL 207.526 on the deed, including family conveyances to a child or grandchild and foreclosure transfers.

Frequently asked questions

Is Walker inside Grand Rapids?

No. Walker is its own Kent County city, formed in 1962. Many addresses carry Grand Rapids ZIP code names for mail.

Must a Walker rental be certified before I sell it?

Not by the city. Walker has no rental certification program, but the 2021 property maintenance code applies and enforcement follows complaints.

What dates matter for Walker property taxes?

Due dates are September 14 for the summer bill and February 14 for the winter bill, by 5 p.m. Unpaid real property tax goes to the Kent County Treasurer on March 1.

Does Walker have a city income tax?

Yes: 1% for residents and one-half of 1% for non-residents, handled by the Walker Income Tax Department.

What are Walker home values?

For 2020 through 2024, owner-occupied homes had a median value of $295,200 and median rent was $1,202.

What a Norton Shores homeowner should sort out before selling

Two offices handle a Norton Shores house: the city, which mails the tax bills and writes the fee schedule, and Muskegon County, which assesses the property and records the deed. Knowing which one answers which question saves a week of phone calls.

The 2025 estimate of 25,088 people is 0.2% above the 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 there are 9,867 households, 84.2% of them in owner-occupied homes, with a median value of $234,800 and a median gross rent of $1,341. Median household income is $76,579, and 90.9% of residents had not moved in the past year, so a house that lists is often one that has been owned a long time. Long-time owners should expect buyers to ask about updates to the roof, furnace and windows, and about any permits for additions.

Where Norton Shores sits

The city fills the southwest corner of Muskegon County, with Lake Michigan to the west and Ottawa County to the south. Muskegon, Roosevelt Park and Muskegon Heights adjoin it on the north. Mona Lake fills the north, Little Black Lake lies in the south, and Hoffmaster State Park protects forested dunes along the shore in the west. ZIP codes 49441, 49444 and 49456 serve the city.

Mona Shores Public Schools serves the city. Commutes average 20.3 minutes. Put the lake, the park or the school district in your listing text wherever it applies to your street, because buyers here often search by those names.

How a Norton Shores property tax bill is built

Muskegon County's assessor sets a value for each parcel every year using mass appraisal, and the city treasurer mails the bills. Assessed value is half of market value, while taxable value, which is what the millage applies to, can run lower.

Norton Shores property tax calendar

Summer bills mailedJuly 1

Millage is charged per thousand dollars of taxable value. Taxable value climbs by the lesser of 5% or inflation until a sale. The following year it resets to the state equalized value, about half of market value, which is why new owners often see a bill above what you paid. A principal residence exemption can take as much as 18 mills of school operating tax off the bill, and a buyer must file for it separately.

Can a Norton Shores owner defer taxes or pay in different ways?

Some owners can defer summer taxes: seniors, people with permanent and total disabilities, blind residents, eligible service members, and qualified surviving spouses. The household income cap for a summer deferment is $40,000 a year.

Applications are available at the Finance Office, 4814 Henry Street, and must reach the treasurer by September 15. Selling in the same year? Ask the treasurer how a deferred balance gets cleared at closing.

The city accepts payment online without registration, by phone at 231.798.6805 with a 2.8% fee on cards and none on ACH, by mail, at City Hall, or in the grey drop box left of the entrance. State law says a bill that never arrived does not cancel a late charge, so call the treasurer if July or December passes quietly.

Zoning and rental fees

The fee schedule adopted March 3, 2026 sets a $2,000 charge for a new or renewed short-term rental registration. A buyer with vacation-rental plans will ask about that number first.

  • Zoning verification letter: $25, confirming how a parcel is zoned, which a buyer's lender or attorney may request.
  • Variance, residential or non-residential: $300 each.
  • Three or more reinspection visits for one violation: $150.
  • Tax roll request: $150.

Check with the Building Division at City Hall, 4814 Henry Street, about permits, open violations and any long-term rental inspection that applies to your house. The City Clerk's list also includes a $35 residential business registration, so a seller who runs a business from the house should ask the Clerk what happens to that registration after a sale.

What a deed costs to record

Muskegon County records the deed for $30 a document. A warranty deed also requires a $5 certificate from the County Treasurer's Office.

Combined state and county transfer tax is $4.30 per $500 of price. A deed from parent to child is exempt under MCL 207.526, as is a deed given in foreclosure.

Two seller steps pay off early. If the house was your principal residence, file the exemption rescission within 90 days of moving out. And confirm every tax bill is paid so the county certificate is not delayed.

Which way of selling a Norton Shores house works best?

You can list, sell by owner, or take a cash purchase. A listing tends to fit a house in good shape, while a cash purchase fits a firm deadline or a house needing work.

  • Before listing: pull your deed, the last two tax bills and permits for any addition or finished basement.
  • Before a rental sale: check whether a short-term registration was ever filed, since the $2,000 fee covers new and renewed ones.
  • Before a cash sale: compare the offer with your likely net after repairs, agent costs and carrying costs.

Give us the Norton Shores address and a note on the house's condition, and we will make an offer you can weigh against a listing.

The closing steps in order

First, call the treasurer to confirm both tax bills are paid and ask about any deferred balance. Second, ask the Building Division about permits and open violations. Third, if the buyer's lender wants proof of how the parcel is zoned, order a zoning verification letter from the city. Fourth, have the title company request the $5 certificate for a warranty deed and record the deed for $30. After closing, rescind your exemption inside 90 days. A cash buyer takes the house as it stands and does not need a lender's appraisal, which keeps the timeline short and the closing date firm.

Bring your deed, the last two tax bills and any permit paperwork to your first conversation with a buyer or title company. If you ever filed a short-term rental registration, say so up front, because the $2,000 fee applies to new and renewed ones and a buyer will ask. If you run a business from the house, ask the City Clerk about the $35 residential business registration. Finally, keep your own copy of every form you sign at closing, including the deed and the rescission, so you can answer any later question from the city or the county.

Frequently asked questions

Which office sets a Norton Shores property's value?

The Muskegon County Assessor's Office sets it each year. The city treasurer handles the billing.

When must Norton Shores summer taxes be paid?

By August 31 to avoid interest. Bills mail July 1, and winter bills follow on December 1 with a February 14 due date.

Does a seller's principal residence exemption pass to the buyer in Norton Shores?

No. The buyer files a fresh affidavit, and approval can remove up to 18 mills of school operating tax. The seller should rescind within 90 days of moving out.

What is the Norton Shores charge for a short-term rental registration?

$2,000 for a new or renewed registration, under the fee schedule adopted March 3, 2026.

What transfer tax does a Norton Shores seller owe?

Combined state and county tax is $4.30 per $500 of value. Some transfers, such as parent to child, are exempt.
